1.note: Berserker's Call locks him down where Blink can't save him, and Axe's low mana means Mana Void barely hurts back.
Fiend's Grip pierces spell immunity and stops Blink or Manta outright, and Enfeeble makes him easier to disable and burst.
Glimpse yanks him back after he Blinks away, and Static Storm shuts Blink down entirely.
Doom silences him out of Blink and deals pure damage past Counterspell, though a well-timed Counterspell can reflect it back.
Soulbind plus Phantom's Embrace can lock him out of casting anything at all.
Duel removes both Blink and Counterspell from the fight, and Blade Mail punishes his low health.
Moon Glaives chew through him before he affords defensive items, and a mistimed Blink lets Eclipse finish him.
Stacked Earthbinds can lock him down almost indefinitely, and the clones barely spend mana so Mana Void whiffs.
Counterspell doesn't stop Sacred Arrow, and Blink's cooldown is too slow to dodge Leap, especially with the Aghanim's Shard charge.
Crippling Fear shuts him down early, and his low mana means Mana Void barely scratches Night Stalker.
Arcane Orb ignores Counterspell as pure damage, and Sanity's Eclipse punishes his low intelligence hard.
His low health is easy prey for Coup de Grace while Blink is on cooldown, and Blur blocks Mana Break outright.
Waning Rift silences him out of Blink (Manta can cleanse it), and Dream Coil with Aghanim's locks him down for a long time.
Purely physical damage skips Counterspell, and both his stuns deny Blink -- Bash of the Deep even through Black King Bar.
Pounce denies Blink, and Essence Shift permanently drains his agility over the course of the game.
Disruption sets up a chain disable and boosts illusion damage via Mana Break; with Aghanim's, Demonic Purge strips both Mana Break and Counterspell.
Refraction shrugs off his low burst, and Meld's damage plus armor shred can end him before he Blinks away.
His root, attack speed and blind make him very hard to solo, and his low mana means Mana Void barely scratches him.
Strong early harassment punishes him before he's farmed, and Nethertoxin disables both Mana Break and Counterspell.
He easily Blinks out of Cold Feet, and Counterspell cuts down spell damage while Ancient Apparition's low mobility feeds Mana Void.
Mana Break drains the mana Abaddon needs for Aphotic Shield, and Counterspell softens Aphotic Shield/Mist Coil damage.
He Blinks straight through Magnetic Field's protection, and his mobility handles a split-pushing Tempest Double.
Mana Break eats his small mana pool before he can spam abilities, and Blink kites him easily since he has no mobility of his own.
He can Blink into or straight out of Power Cogs, negating the initiation entirely.
Counterspell blunts Dragon Tail's follow-up damage.
Echo Stomp and Earth Splitter's long cast times give him plenty of time to Blink away.
Mana Break tears through Mana Shield especially once he has Manta, and Blink dodges Stone Gaze then reinitiates after.
Counterspell shrugs off his all-magic kit, Manta dispels Ignite, and his huge mana pool feeds both Mana Break and Mana Void.
Manta dispels the slows, and Blink lets him sit right next to Supernova to burn the egg down fast.
Counterspell resists his all-magic kit, Manta dispels Decrepify, and his big mana pool means Mana Break/Void hit hard.
Mana Break drains his low mana before Spell Steal triggers, Blink runs him down easily, and he has nothing worth stealing from Anti-Mage.
Blink dodges Spectral Dagger, Counterspell blunts Dispersion and Radiance burn, and Manta stops Desolate from ever landing.
Ball Lightning's mana cost feeds Mana Void, Mana Break clips his mobility, and Counterspell guts his all-magic damage.
Counterspell blunts Gush and Ravage, Blink escapes Anchor Smash, and Mana Break drains his small pool right through Kraken Shell.
He just Blinks away from or onto Tombstone and destroys it, so the zombies rarely matter.
Counterspell softens his damage-over-time kit, and Blink is an easy out from his slows.
Counterspell can bounce Focus Fire's damage back at her, and his late-game items both escape and bypass Windrun.
Mana Break drains his small pool so Reincarnation can't recharge, and Blink kites a hero with zero innate mobility.
Counterspell guts his all-magic damage, and Blink closes the distance on someone with zero mobility of his own.

10.note: Ice Blast stops his Attribute Shift sustain and pushes him toward the shatter threshold, and Ice Vortex's slow plus magic amp sets up early kills.
Counterspell blunts his Waveform/Adaptive Strike combo and can reflect Adaptive Strike back at him, and Mana Break with Manta quickly strips his mana.
Magnetic Field protects buildings from his push, a well-itemized Arc Warden (Orchid/Bloodthorn) is dangerous, and Flux breaks Linken's before Spark Wraith finishes the combo.
Geomagnetic Grip's silence goes through Linken's Sphere and shuts down his escapes, and Boulder Smash/Rolling Boulder lock him down hard.
Natural Order cuts into the armor his agility shift provides, though its short range means a careful Morphling can still burst him down.
Mana Drain starves his low mana pool and Hex denies his key spells outright, and a landed Earth Spike into Finger of Death bursts him hard if he's shifted to agility.
Earthbind locks him in place long enough for Poof stacks to add up.
Sacred Arrow's long stun denies his escape spells, Moonlight Shadow sets up ambushes on him while pushing, and a Linken's Sphere Mirana blocks his single-target tools.
Arcane Orb's pure damage bypasses his agility-shift armor, and Sanity's Eclipse punishes his low pool before he can shift to strength.
His illusion swarm overwhelms Morphling outright, especially with a Diffusal Blade draining his mana, and Doppelganger dodges Adaptive Strike while Eye of Skadi negates his sustain.
Spell Stealing Attribute Shift keeps the stat change permanently, and Waveform gives Rubick a strong nuke/escape.
Arcane Bolt chips him down consistently and disables Linken's, Ancient Seal denies his whole kit, and Mystic Flare with a stun can burst him fast.
A great Morph target -- copying Rage grants spell immunity plus a speed boost, and his high armor blunts Lifestealer's attacks.
Waveform dodges Rupture outright, and Manta dispels Blood Rite's silence.
Waveform escapes Power Cogs, and Attribute Shift's strength buffer lets him survive the duration even if trapped.
Waveform closes the gap fast, and Manta dispels Gust's silence.
Waveform ignores Spirit Bear entirely, and his nukes burst Lone Druid down if not rooted first.
His high agility gives him enough natural armor that Coup de Grace struggles to punch through.
His whole kit lets him dodge Focus Fire, and her low armor folds to his damage.
Waveform breaks Static Link outright, or he can just Morph into Razor and use it back.
His mobility closes the gap on a hero that wants distance, and Sniper's total lack of disables leaves him free to combo.

100.note: Mana Break punishes his low mana pool hard, Blink dodges an incoming Snowball, and Counterspell can reflect it back.
Sticky Napalm makes holding the lane hard, and an ill-timed Snowball gives Batrider a free counter-Lasso if he's out of stun range.
Glimpse pulls him back after a Snowball, and Static Storm, muting items too with Aghanim's, denies the escape entirely.
Boulder Smash returns him after an initiation, and Geomagnetic Grip denies a Snowball escape.
Echo Slam punishes a bunched-up Snowball group hard, setting up prime Blink-Echo-Slam opportunities.
Doppelganger/Manta both dodge an incoming Snowball, and his usual Diffusal Blade punishes Tusk's small mana pool badly.
Blink dodges an incoming Snowball or Ice Shards just like Anti-Mage.
Static Link drains his base damage and cuts Walrus Punch's crit output, and Plasma Field/Eye of the Storm chase him down after a Snowball.
Snowball leaves him unable to steer, letting Techies roll him straight onto mines.
His low mobility and health make him easy Walrus Punch prey, and Walrus Punch can cancel a Fiend's Grip if he isn't the target.
Snowball negates and protects allies from Rupture.
Her low health and armor are easy Walrus Punch prey, and Snowball can protect allies or cancel a Freezing Field channel entirely.
Walrus Punch makes her lose Duel easily unless she's carrying Blade Mail, and Snowball can protect a Duelled ally from taking damage for much of its duration.
His low health and reliance on channeled spells make him vulnerable early, though he can win a straight 1v1 later.
His lack of mobility and low base health make him easy early gank prey.
Snowball closes his long range easily even wasting Shrapnel, and Walrus Punch's huge damage can one-shot his low health and armor.
Snowball saves allies, or himself, from Venomous Gale/Poison Nova, and his low mobility and health make him easy Walrus Punch prey.

Snowball wastes his mana on a dodged Viper Strike, the break is irrelevant since he has no passives, and it can't even disable Walrus Punch since that's an autocast -- his natural Silver Edge also strips Corrosive Skin's resistance.
Tag Team overwhelms his low armor and slow speed, Snowball can save a Dismembered ally and cancel the hook, and Walrus Punch removes a big health chunk while stunning him.
Walrus Punch kicks him straight out of Wukong's Command, wasting the ultimate.

101.note: Mana Break drains and damages him hard, Blink closes the gap for a right-click kill or escapes into fog, a well-timed Counterspell reflects Ancient Seal/Arcane Bolt back onto him, his big mana pool feeds Mana Void, and Anti-Mage's common Black King Bar/Manta dispel Ancient Seal/Concussive Shot.

His low armor and agility gain let stacked Burning Spears burn him down fast at any stage, Berserker's Blood grants attack speed, magic resistance, and regen as Huskar tanks the harass, and Life Break's gap-close, worse with an Aghanim's Inner Fire slow, denies an escape.
Aphotic Shield can dispel a silence, slow, or stun mid-cast, foiling a full Mystic Flare, and Borrowed Time makes him nearly unkillable while even healing off the burst.
Nether Ward makes casting spells nearly suicidal for his low health pool -- though his burst still punishes Pugna hard if the ward gets destroyed, and Decrepify does nothing to save him.
Refraction tanks all his damage, and a single Meld strike can one-shot him.
His low health and lack of armor make him easy Vendetta prey, and Mind Flare turns his own high intelligence against him -- though Spiked Carapace gives Nyx some cover against his spells.
His mana-hungry combo usually leaves him drained right as Reincarnation triggers, letting Wraith King finish him off on the second life.
His nuke-and-silence kit wins the lane outright and lets him quickly finish a squishy target.

Ancient Seal amplifies magic damage, his real weakness, and denies a Timber Chain escape for up to 6 seconds, and he rarely itemizes against silences early -- Reactive Armor doesn't even trigger on magic damage, so a Pipe of Insight barely helps.

He rarely itemizes against silences either, an Orchid usually lands first, a countering Eul's can be turned back with his own silence, and a Rod of Atos-plus-silence combo leaves him with no good answer regardless of which he dispels -- his Black King Bar answer also costs a lot of snowball gold.
Untouchable is useless against constant Arcane Bolts, and Ancient Seal's magic amplification punishes her already-lowest strength gain in the game hard.

Repeated Arcane Bolts harass him hard in lane, and Ancient Seal turns a self-stunning Unstable Concoction into an easy Mystic Flare setup -- though a farmed Radiance-Manta Alchemist can send illusions to force Skywrath out instead.

Both can trade kills fast, but Arcane Bolt's range and low cooldown harasses her hard in lane, Ancient Seal denies a Phantom Strike engage or escape, and Mystic Flare's burst nukes her down early-mid.
Ancient Seal wins the fight outright since she has no answer to silences and depends entirely on her spells, and her short attack range lets him bully the lane easily.

Cold Embrace sets up a perfect Mystic Flare, Ancient Seal's 6-second silence shuts down a fellow spellcaster hard, and she has to approach a fight to land Winter's Curse -- though his terrible armor makes him a real risk to be Cursed himself.

102.note: Ice Blast nullifies healing from both Borrowed Time and Mist Coil, and Aphotic Shield can't dispel it.
Culling Blade's instant-kill threshold bypasses Borrowed Time entirely.
Cyclone wastes Borrowed Time's duration entirely if used the moment he activates it, and Drunken Brawler/Thunder Clap make landing Curse of Avernus' silence hard.
Doom locks out Mist Coil, Aphotic Shield, and Borrowed Time's active half, and an Aghanim's Doom even breaks Curse of Avernus and Borrowed Time's passive healing, leaving his allies exposed.
Her common Eul's wastes some of Borrowed Time's duration before a follow-up Laguna Blade.
Astral Imprisonment wastes Borrowed Time's duration, and Sanity's Eclipse can kill him outright before it even triggers given his low intelligence.

An Aghanim's Demonic Purge disables Curse of Avernus and Borrowed Time's passive half, worse paired with a silence to stop it triggering at all, and even without Aghanim's, Disruption alone wastes Borrowed Time -- Curse of Avernus even works fully on the resulting illusion.
Poison Attack's near-zero cooldown makes Aphotic Shield a weak dispel, and Viper Strike can block Borrowed Time's passive activation and Curse of Avernus outright.
Exorcism and Spirit Siphon both continuously heal him through an active Borrowed Time, and neither can be turned off.
Sacred Arrow's stun is instantly dispelled by Aphotic Shield.
Nightmare and Fiend's Grip are both instantly dispelled by Aphotic Shield, and his own lack of mobility makes Curse of Avernus' silence crippling.
Sticky Napalm, Flaming Lasso, and Flamebreak are all instantly dispelled by Aphotic Shield, and Firefly continuously heals Abaddon under Borrowed Time.
Primal Roar is instantly dispelled by Aphotic Shield, as are Wild Axes' debuff and the Boar's poison.
Aphotic Shield nullifies his combo and clears his creeps at the same time.

Aphotic Shield makes allies far less likely to die to a mine field, and a frequent stack of Remote Mines will always trigger Borrowed Time, making him nearly unkillable by mines alone unless his resistances are lowered or he's broken; the shield also clears Stasis Trap's long root while protecting against the other mines.
If Ruptured, he can just activate Borrowed Time and heal freely by simply moving.
Unless silenced, Borrowed Time lets him escape a Reaper's Scythe during its delay.
Unless broken, Borrowed Time wastes a Duel entirely since it has a shorter cooldown and heals Abaddon for the whole duration while she's forced to keep attacking.
Impale and Spiked Carapace's stun are both instantly dispelled by Aphotic Shield, and Borrowed Time heals him off Nyx's own burst damage.

103.note: Earth's passive spell immunity lets him walk into Echo Stomp's radius and stun with Hurl Boulder, and Storm's Cyclone cancels a channeling Echo Stomp outright.
Battery Assault's mini-stuns punish his poor cast animation, though a channeling Echo Stomp is also a good Hookshot setup if timed right.
Frost Shield offsets Natural Order's armor reduction.
A well-ranged disable chain can cancel Echo Stomp, and Mana Drain punishes his already-low mana.
Blade Fury dodges his stun entirely, though Earth Splitter still pierces spell immunity.
Untouchable cuts his physical damage hard without spell immunity, Enchant purges Astral Spirit's buff the same way, and Nature's Attendants can save her if she survives the combo and jukes clear.
Any of his stuns interrupt a channeling Echo Stomp, Fissure especially given its long range, and a chain-stun usually spells certain death for a spell-reliant Elder Titan.

He has no disengage for a well-timed Echo Stomp, clones count as full heroes for a huge Astral Spirit buff, his mediocre strength gain is prime Natural Order bait, and his clone-clumping playstyle is easy to disable all at once.

Natural Order guts the armor he gets from Attribute Shift (Agility), catching him mid-shift with a stun, silence, or burst punishes it hard, and Blade Mail is devastating against his own attacks or magic combo while under Natural Order.

His lack of disables struggles to stop a channeling Echo Stomp though Manta/Doppelganger dodge the long cast times, his high agility and low strength are ideal Natural Order bait, Echo Stomp/Earth Splitter clear his illusion wave, and even a Heart of Tarrasque build just eats more Earth Splitter damage.

Natural Order denies the armor he'd otherwise gain from stolen agility via Essence Shift, Echo Stomp/Earth Splitter hit him through Shadow Dance, and his relatively low stat gain leaves him squishy without agility-based armor.

His high base armor and reliance on Ultimate Orb items, Manta and Skadi, get gutted by Natural Order, especially dangerous combined with his low health, and his illusions clumping in fights feed Echo Stomp.

As an agility hero with an agility-item build, Natural Order strips his armor and weakens Corrosive Skin's magic resistance badly, and Echo Stomp/Earth Splitter's mixed damage brings him down fast -- an Aghanim's Scepter may be needed to push through Nethertoxin's break.

104.note: Aphotic Shield/Mist Coil make finishing off his allies mid-Duel hard, and Borrowed Time makes Abaddon nearly unkillable in a Duel while healing him since she can't stop attacking.
Magnetic Field denies an easy Duel win.
Enfeeble/Nightmare/Fiend's Grip all deny a Duel win, especially with Bane carrying Blink Dagger.
Untouchable's attack-speed slow makes her one of the hardest Duel targets even through spell immunity, and Impetus/Enchant can help an ally win a Duel against her instead.
Shallow Grave denies a Duel kill outright, and Shadow Wave both heals the ally and damages Legion during the Duel.
Astral Imprisonment denies a Duel kill outright.
A tethered ally is much harder to kill in Duel, and Relocate cancels the Duel and saves them entirely.

A pre-cast Eclipse usually denies a Duel win if she's the target, and Eclipse/Lucent Beam can help an ally win against her instead -- though a smart Legion carries Black King Bar to block them or Aghanim's to reduce the damage.
Facing each other in Duel massively boosts Bulwark's effectiveness, and Spear of Mars/God's Rebuke push her away mid-Duel against an ally.
Mana Shield makes her very hard to burst down in a Duel, and Stone Gaze stops Legion from Duelling at all regardless of target.
Purification denies the kill and always lands during a Duel, and Guardian Angel wastes the whole Duel, worse with Aghanim's saving an ally across the map.

Fate's Edict blocks her attacks briefly, potentially saving the target, Fortune's End dispels Press the Attack's buff and Overwhelming Odds' speed, and False Promise denies both the kill and the bonus damage.

Lucky Shot's disarm and armor-reduction cut her win chance, worse if cast on an ally, a well-timed Rolling Thunder can bait her into a wasted Duel chase, and dueling him is generally a mistake unless he's already low with an ally nearby -- an Aghanim's Legion still risks the full 8 seconds for nothing.
Decrepify on either combatant stops a Duel from completing, and Life Drain can win the fight for Pugna's team by killing Legion or healing her target.

Static Link drains her stacked damage advantage and denies a Duel win, Storm Surge's speed makes him and allies hard to catch, and a pre-cast Eye of the Storm always lands during the forced-proximity Duel.
Mystic Flare bursts her down mid-Duel easily.

God's Strength makes him one of the worst Duel targets, Storm Hammer interrupts a Duel outright, and Warcry's passive-plus-active defense buffs nearby allies significantly, even more with Aghanim's Shard.
Atrophy Aura's percent damage reduction cuts her output even after winning Duels, and she can't dodge Firestorm while forced stationary.
Fury Swipes gives him the edge in a Duel, and Enrage's instant cast lets him take almost no damage right before she initiates -- though Duel denies him casting it at the worst moment for her.
Gravekeeper's Cloak absorbs most of a Duel's damage, and Familiar chain-stuns can deny the win outright.

Cold Embrace saves an ally from dying in Duel, and Winter's Curse turns her damage against her own team -- though she lanes poorly against Legion since Press the Attack strips her debuffs, and rarely survives being Duelled herself.
Paralyzing Cask saves an ally from Duel until she affords Aghanim's, Voodoo Restoration heals through it, and Death Ward helps an ally win if he isn't the target.
Her poor resistance to burst and low mobility make her vulnerable to his multi-target aggression.
Counterspell offers zero protection against Duel, and one successful lockdown is usually enough for her team to finish him before Blink saves him.
Duelling forces him to face her head-on, denying his rear damage reduction passive entirely.
Overwhelming Odds scales huge against a stacked spiderling swarm, and Duel reliably locks her down before she can flee into the treeline.

His fragility and low mobility make him easy Duel bait, Overwhelming Odds/Moment of Courage punish his creep army's numbers, and enough Duel-stack damage can kill his allies before Hand of God saves them.
His physical burst is nearly suicidal to use on her since it invites an instant Duel she's naturally built, Blade Mail, to punish, and Duel locks him down long enough to deny a Skeleton Walk escape.
Her low mobility and lack of defenses make her easy gank bait, and Duelling her strips Marksmanship for a near-guaranteed loss.
Life Break on her is nearly suicidal given her natural Blade Mail, and his low survivability and low-health playstyle make him easy prey for her burst.
Duel's long duration denies a Vendetta escape, and with Aghanim's she can even bypass Spiked Carapace.
His low mobility and lack of defenses make him easy gank prey all game, worse once he's picked up a Blink Dagger to close on.
Duel's long duration denies a Sunder health-swap, and Overwhelming Odds hits his illusions hard.

His frailty and low mobility make him easy Duel bait, Corrosive Skin doesn't protect against her physical attacks, Press the Attack dispels Poison Attack, and Overwhelming Odds' speed easily outruns his slows.
Duel's long duration denies both a Time Lapse and a Shukuchi escape.

105.note: Borrowed Time's auto-trigger usually survives a mine field or Blast Off combo, though a single mine can still finish him at low HP, and Aphotic Shield easily breaks an Ethereal Blade combo.
Counterspell gives him a real chance to survive a Blast Off combo, and his natural Manta dispels the silence and lets him blink away.
Untargeted Exorcism ghosts auto-clear revealed mines as she walks by, and her natural Eul's lets her escape a Blast Off initiation easily.
He can trigger mines safely during Blade Fury and simply walk off during a Blast Off silence if Blade Fury is already up, and Omnislash ignores a Reactive Tazer disarm entirely.
Rage clears mines without taking damage and lets him hit anyone Tazer'd.
Corrosive Skin resists his magic damage, and though a Reactive Tazer disarm blocks Poison Attack, his other abilities still do plenty of damage back.
Dark Ascension flies over mines safely, Crippling Fear stops a Blast Off cast, and Void chases him away from mine safety.

Fate's Edict's full magic resistance blocks most of his damage, Fortune's End dispels Reactive Tazer's buff though the disarm still triggers instantly and clears Blast Off's silence, Ethereal Blade, Proximity Mines' resist-shred, and one instance of Sticky Bomb's slow.
Refraction safely soaks a mine field or absorbs a full Blast Off combo.
Skeletons from Vampiric Spirit keep chokepoints and runes clear of mines, and he'll happily walk through a field whenever Reincarnation is up.

Mines placed near trees catch him jumping, and Blast Off destroys the trees around him for a stun-then-silence combo, while the cooldown between jumps forces him to eat mine damage or bail with Primal Spring.
His huge magic damage bypasses Untouchable, and Blast Off's silence shuts off her ability-reliant damage and healing.
His AoE handles the Phantasm army well, Blast Off silences him out of his disables so allies can walk away from the burst, and Reactive Tazer disarms his illusions even through Black King Bar.
His usually-low max health from shifting into agility, combined with Blast Off's silence, denies both Waveform and Adaptive Strike (Strength), leaving him defenseless.

106.note: Sticky Napalm punishes his low health and melee range hard in lane, and Flaming Lasso is devastating against a hero whose whole kit is locked behind abilities.
He can't safely approach the creep wave with Huskar denying it, and Burning Spear plus close range shut Ember down entirely.
A QW build's EMP burns his small mana pool fast, and Tornado strips Flame Guard so Invoker's magic damage gets through cleanly.
Earth Spike/Hex lock him down hard, Finger of Death's burst punishes his low health, and a Blink Dagger lets Lion punish an overextension or initiate outright.

The bear's huge health and Spirit Link regen make Sleight of Fist nearly useless in lane, letting Lone Druid push him off freely, and Entangling Claws/Savage Roar completely deny a Fire Remnant escape.
Shadowraze strips Flame Guard and kills him fast given his low health, and Necromastery's physical damage is a real weakness for him.
Global Silence/Last Word deny a Fire Remnant escape, and Glaives of Wisdom's pure damage ignores Flame Guard while Arcane Curse out-cools it in lane.

Electric Vortex adds an extra disable, Overload's slow plus Static Remnant burns through Flame Guard fast, a common Orchid seals the deal, and Ball Lightning both initiates from anywhere and dodges Sleight of Fist.

Time Dilation guts his Sleight-of-Fist spam, Chronosphere is reliable lockdown even if Fire Remnant sometimes dodges it, and Time Walk negates Sleight of Fist's damage entirely -- his natural Diffusal Blade also burns mana that Flame Guard can't block, denying an escape if he survives.
Purification's pure damage helps kill him fast, Guardian Angel saves allies from Sleight of Fist, and he rarely itemizes an Orchid to answer it.
Arcane Orb's pure damage kills him fast, and Astral Imprisonment fully negates Flame Guard/Searing Chains while briefly saving OD from Sleight of Fist.
Vendetta lets Nyx close in safely while he farms under Flame Guard, then Spiked Carapace-into-Impale gives a long, reliable disable.
X Marks the Spot denies a Fire Remnant escape until he affords a Eul's or Linken's.
Fire Remnant escapes a Rupture cleanly.

He clears the lane fast trading through Flame Guard, forcing Earth Spirit to gank early without enough gold or levels, and Sleight of Fist dodges his whole kit -- a Black King Bar even lets him combo Sleight of Fist with Searing Chains to catch and kill Earth Spirit.
Flame Guard and Searing Chains punish his fragile early clones, and a Battle Fury cleave on Sleight of Fist devastates a crowded clone group later.
His evasive kit dodges close encounters and Reality Rift's slow, and Flame Guard/Sleight of Fist tear through the Phantasm illusion army fast.
Flame Guard absorbs a large chunk of her magic damage, and Sleight of Fist dodges Dragon Slave/Light Strike Array.
Sleight of Fist devastates his illusion army, he has no way to stop a Fire Remnant, and Ember's long range plus wide kit rarely gives him a clean Sunder window.
Her fragility and lack of a real disable leave her helpless, and Flame Guard blocks her whole damage kit while Searing Chains/Flame Guard/Sleight of Fist burst her down.

Flame Guard plus a Battle Fury clears Nature's Call's treants easily, he has multiple ways to escape Sprout, and Activate Fire Remnant destroys Sprout's trees while Searing Chains interrupts a Teleportation.
Sleight of Fist with a Battle Fury is the natural counter to his illusion army.

Searing Chains/Flame Guard quickly burn through Refraction to expose her low health, he has no way to stop a Fire Remnant escape, and Searing Chains gives true sight into Meld while denying a Blink Dagger escape.
Laning against him means eating Sleight of Fist given his low health, and Arc Lightning's chip damage gets nullified by Flame Guard.

107.note: Aphotic Shield is a strong dispel against his whole kit including Magnetize, and Borrowed Time makes him nearly unkillable.

He clears the lane fast trading through Flame Guard, forcing Earth Spirit to gank early without enough gold or levels, and Sleight of Fist dodges his whole kit -- a Black King Bar even lets Ember combo Sleight of Fist with Searing Chains to catch and kill him.
Shapeshift's speed lets Lycan chase him down.
Dream Coil/Waning Rift both deny his escape options off his own Rolling Boulder.
Pounce's root denies a Rolling Boulder escape, making him easy to shut down especially in lane.
His ranged attacks and Static Remnant win the lane and out-level him, and Electric Vortex can kill him fast unless Storm has bought a Falcon Blade to survive Earth Spirit's own damage.
Battery Assault disables Rolling Boulder, Power Cogs traps him in place, and Hookshot-plus-Rocket Flare chases him down with vision.

Landing Rolling Boulder on his own Stone Remnant breaks Life Drain's range requirement, Geomagnetic Grip shuts down a spell-reliant Pugna's whole kit, magic damage kills through Decrepify fast, worse with Ethereal Blade for a one-hit combo, and his big health pool with Heart of Tarrasque/Bracer shrugs off Nether Ward.
Long-range disables from Stone Remnant and Rolling Boulder disrupt a Dismember from a safe distance, with the talent even pulling allies out, and Geomagnetic Grip silences him too.
He's an easy initiation target, especially once he's split-pushing with Boots of Travel, and Stone Remnant/Rolling Boulder's huge range denies a teleport home.
He can gank an early, level-hungry Invoker hard, and his long-range stun-silence combo disrupts a careful Invoke sequence easily.
Magnetize's damage-over-time, refreshable via Stone Remnant, wastes her Refraction charges fast, letting the team burst her down.

Rolling Boulder's huge range interrupts a channeling Black Hole easily since Enigma can't move while casting, forcing an early Black King Bar, and his ganking power punishes a squishy, solo-farming early Enigma.

108.note: Reaper's Scythe/Heartstopper Aura both deal percent-health damage that ignores his high health, and Ghost Shroud both protects Necrophos from Atrophy Aura and amplifies his own healing.

Static Link drains his damage even inside Atrophy Aura's range while boosting Razor's own, and his slow, low-mobility kit can't escape Razor's speed to prevent the max drain and burst -- though Razor has no way to stop a Fiend's Gate escape without disables.

Lunar Blessing's damage and armor helps allies endure Atrophy Aura, Eclipse devastates a team grouped for Fiend's Gate or intercepts arrivals despite Pit of Malice, and an Aghanim's Eclipse can even finish an escaping Underlord.
Glimpse returns an escaping Underlord or ally from Fiend's Gate, and Static Storm/Kinetic Field both lock down his slow, low-mobility kit and can intercept a Fiend's Gate arrival.
X Marks the Spot returns an escaping Fiend's Gate target, and Torrent/Ghostship/an Aghanim's Torrent Storm/a Shard Tidal Wave all excel at intercepting a Fiend's Gate arrival.
Infernal Blade scales hard off his high health, and Doom stops him spamming abilities or using Fiend's Gate to escape at all.

Midnight Pulse punishes his high health hard, and Midnight Pulse/Black Hole can catch his team off guard right as they arrive via Fiend's Gate since Atrophy Aura does nothing to stop it -- though he can interrupt a channeling Black Hole with Pit of Malice or scout Enigma with Firestorm, denying Blink Dagger if Enigma lacks Black King Bar.

His long range keeps him out of Firestorm/Pit of Malice/Atrophy Aura's reach, Assassinate's ministun cancels a Fiend's Gate escape, but the same portal can close the gap on him fast if Underlord brings his team -- and Sniper has little to intercept it outside Shrapnel/an Aghanim's Concussive Grenade.
Arcane Orb deals big damage to his high health, and Sanity's Eclipse tears through his comparatively small mana pool hard.

Winter's Curse/Splinter Blast devastate a team grouped for Fiend's Gate, and Cold Embrace protects allies from Atrophy Aura's damage -- though a Cold-Embraced ally is easy Firestorm/Pit of Malice bait.
His whole kit is easy Spell Steal fodder.

Requiem/Shadowraze still hit hard even trapped in Pit of Malice, Requiem is a great tool to intercept a Fiend's Gate arrival, and Necromastery's stacking damage combined with Presence of the Dark Lord's armor shred lets him punch through Atrophy Aura's reduction.
Fury Swipes bypasses Atrophy Aura's damage reduction entirely, Enrage dispels Pit of Malice's root easily, though he has little to intercept a grouped Fiend's Gate escape besides Earthshock.
Firestorm clears his creeps easily, Pit of Malice traps him helpless, Atrophy Aura punishes every creep kill, and Fiend's Gate counters his pushing with no way for him to intercept it.
Atrophy Aura guts her damage hard since she's entirely agility-reliant.
Atrophy Aura makes winning Duels much harder, and Fiend's Gate either saves an ally from Duel or intercepts her since she has no AoE outside Overwhelming Odds.

Atrophy Aura hurts her farm and Rip Tide damage badly unless she plays a nuker build, and Firestorm clears her illusions -- though Song of the Siren can ambush an unprepared Fiend's Gate arrival, and Aghanim's Ensnare/Reel In deny the escape.
Firestorm/Pit of Malice/Atrophy Aura all punish his illusion army hard, and he has nothing to stop or intercept a Fiend's Gate escape.

Firestorm ignores Blur to damage her in lane, Pit of Malice denies both engage and escape via Phantom Strike, and Atrophy Aura cripples her all-physical damage including Coup de Grace -- she has no good answer to Fiend's Gate either.

Pit of Malice cast in his charge path cancels Charge of Darkness outright, Atrophy Aura guts his all-physical Greater Bash damage, and Fiend's Gate both escapes a gank and ambushes him since he has little to intercept it.

Atrophy Aura significantly cuts his damage even in Metamorphosis, Firestorm/Pit of Malice control him and his illusions, and Fiend's Gate either bails out a bad engagement or catches him off guard -- his only real counter is Reflection.

Firestorm destroys Refraction fast and still hits her in Meld, she struggles to maneuver around Pit of Malice, and Atrophy Aura cuts her all-physical damage -- though her Psionic Traps can intercept and warn against a Fiend's Gate arrival.

109.note: Berserker's Call-into-Counter Helix shreds his low health and illusions fast, Call even pierces his Black King Bar with nothing Manta can dispel, and a permanent-armor-stacking Axe, Blade Mail, Crimson Guard, Assault Cuirass, Shiva's, makes his attacks tickle even during Metamorphosis -- Culling Blade can finish him before Sunder if his health is low.

Crystal Nova/Freezing Field clear his illusion army and can kill him before Black King Bar, he has no way to disable or cancel Freezing Field and dislikes buying the Scythe/Abyssal that would help, and her common Black King Bar/Glimmer/Shadow Blade line denies him a Sunder window.

An Aghanim's Poison Touch instantly kills his whole illusion set and hexes him outright, Shallow Grave saves a Sundered ally since he has no burst outside it, Shadow Wave damages him and illusions whenever Metamorphosis is down, and it pierces his Black King Bar.
Marksmanship pierces his high base armor and clears illusions with Aghanim's, Gust denies a Sunder cast, and he rarely buys the armor that would help against her burst.
Rolling Boulder/Geomagnetic Grip both deny a Sunder cast, and Magnetize's magic damage bypasses his high armor.

Echo Stomp/Astral Spirit set up a team kill before Sunder, Natural Order cripples the armor his low strength gain depends on especially with Ultimate Orb items, and Echo Stomp/Earth Splitter kill both him and his illusions.
He can deal heavy laning damage before Sunder is even up, and Enrage's damage reduction lets him survive a Sunder while making Terrorblade's attacks tickle for its duration.

His wide AoE clears illusion waves and damages the real hero, magic damage bypasses his armor, a common Hurricane Pike outranges Sunder entirely, and an Aghanim's Macropyre pierces Black King Bar -- though a well-timed Sunder can still punish an unprepared Jakiro.
Laguna Blade, worse with the pure-damage talent, can kill him before Sunder, and Dragon Slave/Light Strike Array clear his illusion set.

An Aghanim's Eclipse can finish him before Sunder without Black King Bar, Moon Glaives clears illusions though Reflection can turn them against her in lane, and her common Satanic/Black King Bar/Linken's line protects against or nullifies Sunder -- Monkey King Bar/Revenant's Brooch/Gleipnir also bypass his armor.

Mirror Image easily dispels Reflection while Conjure Image's differently-colored illusions expose the real Terrorblade, an Aghanim's Ensnare/Reel In pierces Black King Bar to separate him from his army, Rip Tide punishes his low health and strength, and Song of the Siren buys time to undo a Sunder -- though her low burst struggles to close it out without Black King Bar or Linken's.

Ether Shock/Mass Serpent Wards damage him and his illusions, Hex denies Sunder or Manta and destroys an illusion, and Shackles disables him with no way to dispel it while healing Shadow Shaman -- an Aghanim's Shackles even summons more wards to pile on damage.

Plasma Field/Eye of the Storm clear his illusions, Static Link and Eye of the Storm both bypass Manta and Black King Bar to cripple his damage and armor, and he needs his own Black King Bar/Linken's to survive long enough for a Sunder.
Sleight of Fist/Flame Guard/Fire Remnant devastate him and his illusions, and he has no disable to stop Ember from escaping since he dislikes Scythe/Abyssal.

Reaper's Scythe can kill him before Sunder since it disables on cast, Ghost Shroud lets Necrophos tank his attacks entirely and amplifies his own healing to outlast a Sunder, his common Radiance/Death Pulse clear illusions, and Terrorblade's all-physical kit does nothing to a Ghost-Shrouded target.
Arcane Orb's pure damage bypasses his armor to wreck him and his illusions fast, and an Aghanim's Astral Imprisonment can even save an ally from a Sunder.

Juxtapose overwhelms his single-target, no-wave-clear kit, Doppelganger dispels Reflection instantly, a natural Diffusal Blade drains the mana he needs for Sunder, and Conjure Image's distinct illusion coloring makes the real Terrorblade easy to spot.

Last Word/Global Silence deny the Sunder he depends on to survive, the Last-Word-Mutes talent even blocks Manta/Black King Bar, Arcane Curse/an upgraded Glaives clear his illusions, and Glaives/Revenant's Brooch bypass his high armor.

An Aghanim's Laser blinds him and his illusions, Laser/Heat-Seeking Missile with Rearm ignore his armor to devastate his low health, and his natural Blink Dagger plus Boots of Travel let him escape and outmaneuver a hero with no disable -- even an Aghanim's Warp Flare can relocate him away entirely.

Whirling Axes' miss chance plus Fervor's attack speed overwhelm him even during Metamorphosis, and Skull Basher/Abyssal Blade deny a Sunder almost entirely -- Battle Trance even nullifies a landed Sunder's effect.

Firestorm damages him and his illusions from a safe distance, Pit of Malice controls them in place, Atrophy Aura cuts his damage significantly even in Metamorphosis, and Fiend's Gate either escapes a bad fight or ambushes him -- forcing an Aghanim's Terror Wave as his only real answer.
Arc Lightning/Lightning Bolt burst him and his illusions fast, and an Aghanim's Static Field auto-hits his whole illusion set regardless of health.
His magic and pure damage combo ignores Terrorblade's armor entirely and clears illusions fast with AoE, and Reactive Armor's regen and armor let him survive even a landed Sunder.
His heavy magic damage bypasses Terrorblade's armor, and Ball Lightning both initiates from range and kites him since he has no disable outside an Aghanim's Terror Wave.
Great Cleave-God's Strength clears illusions fast, Storm Hammer's AoE stuns him and the army together, and Warcry's armor helps the team tank his all-physical damage.
Arcane Bolt punishes his low lane health, Ancient Seal denies a Sunder cast, and Mystic Flare can burst him down before he affords Manta/Black King Bar.

Vendetta's pure damage plus Impale/Mind Flare's magic burst ignore his armor to kill him before Sunder, and his common Urn/Dagon/Meteor Hammer all bypass armor too -- though a farmed Eye of Skadi/Black King Bar Terrorblade shuts down the solo-kill window.

Sticky Bomb/Blast Off/Proximity Mines all bypass his armor to punish his low max health, Sticky Bomb is easy to land on a clumped illusion group, an Aghanim's Reactive Tazer disarms his whole illusion set even through Black King Bar, and Blast Off's stun denies a Sunder cast.
Reflection turns his own Curse of Avernus back on him, silencing and slowing an illusion that can't be killed, only dispelled.
Sunder ignores Ice Blast entirely and still swaps health as normal.

An illusion can absorb and disable Nightmare, and his illusion army muddies a Fiend's Grip target -- though Aghanim's Brain Sap or a farmed Mjollnir help Bane pick out the real one, and Conjure Image's distinct coloring is a tell unless he's bought Manta.
His single-target damage-over-time kit and lack of disables let Terrorblade almost always get a Sunder off, and Corrosive Skin doesn't stop physical damage, so Metamorphosis kills him fast.

Reflection and Metamorphosis exploit its weak durability hard, and Reflection punishes Overcharge by damaging and slowing both Io and its tethered ally -- though only an Aghanim's Terror Wave stops a Tether/Relocate escape.

Reflection spreads Presence of the Dark Lord's armor reduction onto him, and his lack of survivability or escape leaves him easy prey, especially if he builds physical damage into Terrorblade's high armor.
His low armor and mobility make him easy right-click prey, illusions muddy a Meat Hook, and since Dismember is single-target, an illusion can save the real Terrorblade if caught.
Reflection's illusion still carries Mana Break, and he simply can't manfight Terrorblade at any stage of the game.
Sunder saves himself or allies from Assassinate, his high armor blunts Sniper's late-game right-clicks, and a well-farmed Terrorblade simply outcarries him.

A low-health Sunder on her bypasses Dispersion entirely, staying near his illusions denies Desolate's bonus, Reflection turns her own Desolate against her while slowing her, and his high armor resists Dispersion's reflected damage -- he's one of the few heroes who can man-fight her even late.

Reflection's illusion carries Feast too, his low strength gain means Feast can't outheal Terrorblade's damage, Open Wounds is hard to land on the real one among illusions unless Manta is skipped, and his right-click reliance struggles against Terrorblade's high armor.

A well-timed Sunder dodges Maledict's burst, though it can kill him early if he has no target, his high armor resists Death Ward's physical damage though an Aghanim's bouncing Death Ward wipes his illusions, and he has no disable to stop a maxed Death Ward channel.

His high armor gain resists Wraith King's physical damage, WK has no AoE for the illusion army, a common Manta/Diffusal deals with Reincarnation before Aghanim's Shard, and a just-Reincarnated WK at low health is easy Sunder bait.

11.note: Berserker's Call and Counter Helix punish him for standing near creeps, and his tankiness/regen shrugs off early Shadowraze damage.
Static Link saps his Necromastery-fueled damage (and can't be blocked by Black King Bar), and Plasma Field/Eye of the Storm melt his low health fast.
Enfeeble stunts his weak early damage and Necromastery stacking, Brain Sap punishes him hard, and Fiend's Grip can remove him from a fight even through Black King Bar.
Shuriken Toss cancels Requiem of Souls, early Jinada/Shadow Walk ganks punish him, and Track denies a Shadow Blade escape.
Glimpse and Kinetic Field set up early kills, and Static Storm cancels a Requiem of Souls cast.
Jungle-creep disables cover his lack of escape tools, and Doom's magic damage combo (often with Radiance) usually kills him before Shadowraze or Requiem can help.
Dragon Tail cancels Requiem of Souls, Breathe Fire cuts his damage further, and his strength/Dragon Blood tank the right-clicks easily.
He gets outharassed by Dual Breath/Liquid Fire despite his own fragility, Ice Path cancels Requiem easily, and Aghanim's Macropyre discourages him from channeling at all.
Her longer attack range wins the lane outright, and her burst combo kills him fast before he can afford a Satanic.

Lucent Beam/Eclipse cancel Requiem without Black King Bar, her farm and physical damage outscale him in lane, and a well-itemized Luna can burst him down even through Black King Bar (though he can fight back with Wind Waker).
Void cancels Requiem, Crippling Fear denies Shadowraze/Requiem entirely, and his tankiness plus Dark Ascension/Gem let him hunt Shadow Fiend down anytime.
Decrepify denies him a kill mid-attack, and Nether Ward punishes him hard for casting Requiem or spamming Shadowraze.
Shrapnel denies a Blink Dagger escape from range, and Take Aim/Headshot let Sniper harass him from outside Shadowraze range.
Charge of Darkness ganks him early before he stacks Necromastery, and it (plus Nether Strike) can deny a Requiem of Souls cast.
Laser denies him a kill mid-attack, Scythe of Vyse denies Requiem, and a maxed Dagon/Ethereal Blade combo can burst him down fast.
Earthshock denies his escape after a Blink Dagger jump, and Overpower/Fury Swipes/Enrage let Ursa simply out-damage him in a straight fight.
Kraken Shell dispels his damage-amp stacks and his own damage-reduction ultimate, and Ravage cancels Requiem without Black King Bar.
Nethertoxin cuts both his damage stacks hard, Corrosive Skin resists his nukes, and Viper Strike/Poison Attack punish his lack of mobility.
Arc Lightning lets Zeus farm safely out of Shadowraze range, Lightning Bolt harasses his last hits, and Thundergod's Wrath can reveal a Shadow Blade escape.
He usually carries a Hurricane Pike to escape Power Cogs easily, and can farm the Cogs themselves for Necromastery stacks.
He can focus down a single clone fast, and his AoE spells punish the whole clone stack.
He farms treants easily for Necromastery stacks, and a Boots of Travel/Shadow Blade build lets him answer a split push directly.
His strong nukes win the lane outright, since Void Spirit can't safely approach the creep wave to farm.
As a right-click carry with a natural Black King Bar, Silencer's spell-based kit does little to him.
Shadow Dance doesn't protect him from Shadow Fiend's AoE spells.

110.note: Void interrupts Icarus Dive, and Crippling Fear's silence shuts down a spellcaster -- though Supernova punishes him back by turning night to day, overriding Dark Ascension's Hunter-in-the-Night bonuses.
Tempest Double is a full unit, not an illusion, effectively halving Supernova's health pool, and Magnetic Field's attack speed lets him shred the egg fast even under Fire Spirits.
Berserker's Blood's attack speed lets him tank down a Supernova easily, and Life Break can chase an Icarus Dive escape if timed right -- though a Shiva's/Spirit Vessel Phoenix has real counterplay.
His burst of attacks destroys Supernova in seconds regardless of Fire Spirits, and Enrage both blunts Phoenix's damage and clears any debuffs.
Global Silence disrupts his initiation, Last Word denies an escape, and repeated deaths near him permanently sap the intelligence Phoenix needs for mana.
His clones are real units, not illusions, so a full clump deals full damage to the Sun -- unlike illusion-based heroes.

Blood Rite's silence and pure damage punish a slow reaction, Rupture turns Icarus Dive into a health-cutting risk with no way to dispel it, and reckless health-cost ability spam feeds Thirst's vision.
Corrosive Skin resists his damage-over-time while punishing him for staying near it, and his own health-cost spells make him easy Poison Attack prey.

His health-cost spells make him increasingly vulnerable to Reaper's Scythe the longer a fight goes, and his no-escape kit means a well-timed stun is basically guaranteed -- though a Scepter Supernova can save an ally from the ultimate.
Lil' Shredder can burst a level-1 Supernova egg in just 6 hits.
His damage-over-time burns through Refraction fast, and Meld can't hide her from his AoE spells.
She can't use Phantom Strike on the Sun, Blur doesn't stop his magic DPS from burning her low health, and the attack-speed slow leaves her unable to retaliate without spell immunity.

Catching her first slows and damages her before she can Duel effectively, Press the Attack dispels the Fire Spirits slow and grants attack speed to shred a Supernova if not careful, and Sun Ray, or a Scepter Supernova, can swing or cancel a Duel entirely.

Icarus Dive/Sun Ray/Supernova all destroy the trees he needs for Tree Dance, and cutting his tree stuns him for 4 seconds and deals heavy damage -- though a farmed, attack-speed Monkey King can win the race if he jumps first.
Fire Spirits disrupt his jungling and can force an early, wasted Hand of God, and his weak creep damage and speed rarely punishes a Supernova cast.

Supernova saves himself, or with Aghanim's an ally, from Echo Slam, his low base attack time and poor agility make destroying the egg hard, Icarus Dive passes through Fissure, and his damage-over-time denies a Blink Dagger initiation for a long stretch.
Supernova, with or without Aghanim's, allows him to save himself or an ally from Ice Blast, and Icarus Dive escapes Cold Feet quickly.
Icarus Dive escapes his kit fast, especially Demonic Purge, and Phoenix's AoE clears Disruption illusions.

111.note: Counterspell blunts his damage and can reflect it, Mana Break/Mana Void overwhelm his mana-reliant kit, and Blink exploits his low mobility for a chase.
False Promise can't save an ally already below Culling Blade's threshold, and Fate's Edict barely protects against Axe's mostly-physical damage.
Fortune's End can't dispel Warpath or Quill Spray stacks, and his damage reduction blunts Oracle's output while risking an accidental Purifying Flames heal on him.

Time Walk/Backtrack negate his burst, Time Dilation punishes his low-cooldown kit and can catch him off guard if Fortune's End is down -- though False Promise plus Fate's Edict is one of the best combos in the game for delaying or saving a Chronosphere target.

Disruption protects Shadow Demon's allies from Fortune's End or lets Shadow Poison land safely on Oracle's own allies, and an Aghanim's Demonic Purge blocks over-time healing like Purifying Flames/Urn for longer or on more targets -- though it can't stop instant heals or auras like Mekansm.
Dispersion blunts his burst, and Fate's Edict's disarm barely matters since she deals damage even without landing hits.
Fate's Edict shuts down his mostly-magic damage early, Fortune's End interrupts a channeling Onslaught, and False Promise plus Fate's Edict/Purifying Flames can fully negate his burst combos.

Fortune's End dispels Flame Guard and Searing Chains, even freezing a Fire Remnant in place, and Fate's Edict's disarm can neutralize Sleight of Fist for several seconds if he lacks a dispel or immunity -- positioning is hard given how far back he plays.
False Promise plus disarm from Fate's Edict can save an ally through a whole Duel, barring an enemy Axe, and Fortune's End dispels her Overwhelming Odds/Press the Attack buffs.

Fortune's End dispels Cursed Crown before it stuns or saves a stunned ally, Fate's Edict negates Bedlam's damage-over-time and Shadow Realm's burst, and Fortune's End clears Terrorize's fear or a fast-cast Bramble Maze root.
Fortune's End dispels Guardian Angel in an area, and Fate's Edict baits and dispels Heavenly Grace.

His low health folds to Oracle's burst, and his rapid-fire, no-cast-point spell combo, especially shift-queued Fortune's End, is hard to Spell Steal -- staying in the backline of a fight also denies the steal window.
False Promise stops an Ice Blast shatter and Fate's Edict blunts its damage-over-time, denying a frostbitten ally counts as an Oracle deny, and Fortune's End dispels Cold Feet before it freezes.
Fortune's End nullifies Arcane Curse/Last Word/Global Silence if timed right, and Fate's Edict's disarm shuts off his Glaives of Wisdom right-click damage.
Fate's Edict blocks or dispels his self-damaging magic kit, and his health-cost casting makes him easy Oracle burst prey.

Fortune's End dispels Ghost Shroud, negating its utility, and Purifying Flames is a strong nuke against a hero who takes bonus magic damage while ethereal, while Fate's Edict fully negates a telegraphed Reaper's Scythe.
Fortune's End dispels both Ion Shell and Surge, letting Oracle control him hard especially in lane.
Fate's Edict negates his all-magic kit and can even trigger Proximity Mines safely, and Fortune's End clears Reactive Tazer or Blast Off's silence while False Promise delays his burst.
Fate's Edict fully negates his heavy magic damage, and Fortune's End dispels Ancient Seal.

112.note: Ice Blast blocks Cold Embrace's healing, turning it into a plain 4-second stun and a perfect Ice Blast setup, and Cold Feet on a Cold-Embraced ally nearly guarantees a freeze.
Cold Embrace is the perfect setup for Chaos Meteor, EMP, or a global Sun Strike.
Cold Embrace doesn't stop Lucent Beam/Eclipse, Moon Glaives won't hit an ally under Winter's Curse, and Luna's better night vision from Lunar Blessing outdoes Arctic Burn.
Guardian Angel fully counters Winter's Curse, and Purification/Repel answer Arctic Burn/Splinter Blast/Winter's Curse well.
Arcane Orb keeps damaging a Cold-Embraced ally regardless, it can't even hit an ally taunted by Winter's Curse, and Astral Imprisonment can protect a Cursed target.
Cold Embrace sets up his whole kit perfectly especially Life Drain, Decrepify can save a Cursed ally by wasting most of its duration, and Nether Ward punishes her mana-hungry kit hard.
Cold Embrace sets up a perfect Mystic Flare, and his 6-second silence shuts down a fellow spellcaster.

Dark Pact dispels Arctic Burn/Splinter Blast though not to escape Pounce, Cold Embrace still lets him stack Essence Shift off attacks against its owner, but his low health makes him a bad Winter's Curse target since it can't be dispelled at all.

Cold Embrace is a great setup for his pure-damage nukes, Reactive Armor tanks a Curse if he's the target while dealing next to nothing if he's cursed to attack an ally, and his common Lotus Orb reflects Winter's Curse back at her.

Cold Embrace sets up his magic and pure nukes well, Winter's Curse is hard to land on him since he stays backline, and his mediocre attack does little if cursed -- Ethereal Blade/Defense Matrix also save a Cursed ally.
Zombies usually outrun her, making Tombstone hard to handle, and a Cold-Embraced ally still takes Decay's magic damage.
Fury Swipes doesn't work on allies under Winter's Curse, gutting most of his damage, and his own Aghanim's Enrage lets him survive her initiation.
Her kit can't effectively interrupt his actions, letting him dominate the fight.
His summons/Inner Beast attack speed punish a Cursed teammate hard, and Cold Embrace mitigates a single-target Primal Roar initiation.

Winter's Curse can make his illusions attack the real Chaos Knight or turn the whole army on an ally, Cold Embrace protects a focused target, Splinter Blast hits illusions, and Arctic Burn punishes his big HP pool and typical lack of magic resistance.
Cold Embrace fully negates his all-physical damage, and Splinter Blast/Winter's Curse punish his creep-heavy playstyle -- catching him mid-Shapeshift near creeps with Winter's Curse is often lethal.
Cold Embrace is very effective against Duel, and Winter's Curse cast on her while she's Duelling stuns her for most of it or turns her damage against a teammate.

Grouped clones make an ideal Winter's Curse target that forces him to kill himself, and he can't protect against it with Linken's like other heroes, while Splinter Blast hits nearly every clone at once.
Cold Embrace protects a focused ally, though Fervor keeps stacking even while it's active.

113.note: None of his kit answers her spiderling swarm well, she thrives in the short games his item-reliance can't keep up with, and he has no disable to stop Insatiable Hunger's lifesteal shredding his low armor.

Forge Spirit negates Flux, a well-timed Chaos Meteor combo bursts him and his double at once, an early Orchid shuts him down hard if Invoker wins the lane, and Deafening Blast/Ice Wall cripple his mobility and damage.

Mana Break punishes his cast-heavy, mana-dependent kit, Blink dodges Flux's slow to close the gap, his farm keeps pace with Tempest Double's push, a common Manta dispels a threatening Bloodthorn, and Counterspell blunts his magic damage -- though jumping him alone once he has Black King Bar risks getting caught between two damage sources.

Magnetic Field doesn't block Berserker's Call or Counter Helix, his high attack speed with Tempest Double feeds Counter Helix hard, and the threat of Call/Blink forces him to play far back, halving his team's damage.

Sticky Napalm harasses him easily given his low durability, Flamebreak pushes him and his double out of Magnetic Field, Firefly-plus-Blink lets Batrider damage both copies while kiting, and Flaming Lasso, worse with Aghanim's hitting both, is brutal since he rarely carries Linken's -- though Spark Wraith scouts Batrider and a common Gleipnir denies his own Blink.

His low armor and mobility make him easy Quill Spray/Viscous Nasal Goo bait, and he rarely justifies a Silver Edge given its opportunity cost -- though against a jump-heavy team it becomes surprisingly strong on him, giving two breaks at once.
Phantasm dispels Flux, and Reality Rift pulls him out of Magnetic Field where his low mobility and lack of a stun leave him stuck.
Divided We Stand cripples Flux's value against the clone swarm, his early power spikes pressure Arc before he can fight effectively, and without Black King Bar, Earthbind-Poof finishes him fast.
Moon Glaives clears Tempest Double easily, and her short range plus speed let her fight him inside his own Magnetic Field.
Mirror Image illusions depush the lanes his double shoves and dispel Flux while resisting its effect.
Smoke Screen plus a Diffusal Blade leaves him nearly helpless given his low mobility to escape the silence, and Tricks of the Trade deals solid damage before he can move out.
Doppelganger dispels Flux, Phantom Rush closes the distance fast, and Juxtapose overwhelms a kit built to punish isolated targets.

Magnetic Field can't stall Nether Blast's tower damage without an Aghanim's Shard, he has no disable for Life Drain/Decrepify, their short cooldowns let Pugna handle both him and his clone, and Pugna thrives in the short games he can't keep up with.
Magnetic Field denies her an easy Duel win.

Flux strips Refraction fast while his superior attack lets him punish freely, Spark Wraith kills the ranged creep to deny her a safe mute spot, a Tempest Double stacking Flux/Spark Wraith can burst her down in seconds even through Meld, and a Bloodthorn/Blink or Hurricane Pike double threatens her split-push hard enough to force an early Black King Bar.
His summons can soak a Sacred Arrow meant for him or an ally, and she rarely builds the armor needed to fight a late-game Arc Warden.
Magnetic Field defends against a Metamorphosis engage, and a common Bloodthorn or Scythe of Vyse locks him out of his kit entirely.
Tempest Double, Magnetic Field's attack speed, and his long range destroy a Supernova far faster than most heroes can.
Magnetic Field's evasion negates his attacks entirely without true strike.
Magnetic Field protects him and allies from her ranged attacks, since entering it costs her the Marksmanship bonus -- though a Marksmanship proc still hits through true strike.
Magnetic Field makes Impetus miss outright, and entering it to land a hit costs her the extra damage from range.

114.note: Firefly gives vision of him in trees while destroying nearby ones to deny jump spots or drop him, Sticky Napalm's turn-rate slow cripples his tree-hopping for Jingu Mastery and reveals him, and Flamebreak/Flaming Lasso can pull him out of Wukong's Command.
Wild Axes chops down his trees, Call of the Wild Hawk scouts him perched above, and Primal Roar stuns him for a long duration even through spell immunity.
Track reveals him even hiding in the trees.
Cinder Brew/Drunken Brawler make Jingu Mastery hard to stack, Cyclone removes him for 6 seconds without a dispel, and Dispel Magic strips Jingu's bonuses.

Thunder Strike reveals him in trees and its periodic damage denies grounded Tree Dance, Glimpse pulls him out mid-escape and can end Wukong's Command early if he's pulled out of its radius -- though once he's already cast the ultimate and struck first, Disruptor's tools do little.
Impetus's pure damage ignores Wukong's Command's armor bonus, Enchant dispels Jingu Mastery, Untouchable denies stacking it at all, and Sproink escapes the ultimate's radius.
Malefice keeps Tree Dance on cooldown and can interrupt Wukong's Command's long cast, and Midnight Pulse destroys a big chunk of trees.
Blinding Light pushes him out of Wukong's Command while blinding him, and Solar Bind punishes his vulnerability to burst -- though he can gank a careless Keeper early-mid in return.
Skewer/Reverse Polarity both push him out of Wukong's Command.
His tree-reliance makes him prime Spear of Mars bait even through a Mischief disguise, and God's Rebuke easily pushes him out of the ultimate's radius.
Blur makes stacking Jingu Mastery hard, Phantom Strike blinks straight to him through the clone circle, and Coup de Grace's burst can end Wukong's Command early by killing him.

Icarus Dive/Supernova destroy the tree he's standing on, Fire Spirits cuts his attack speed to deny Jingu stacking, and a well-placed Supernova next to Wukong's Command forces him to eat massive AoE or step away.
Blink keeps her out of his Jingu-stacking range, and Scream of Pain/Sonic Wave's AoE hits him disguised, treed, or inside his own ultimate.
Ball Lightning catches up fast, destroys nearby trees to cancel Tree Dance, and stuns him in the process.
Mines near trees detect him, and a follow-up Blast Off destroys the tree for high fall damage and a stun.
His cheap, low-cooldown kit destroys the trees Monkey King depends on, and Timber Chain escapes Wukong's Command.
Wave of Terror gives flying vision over trees and can hit and end a Mischief disguise, and Nether Swap cancels Wukong's Command by swapping him out of the circle.
His poison damage-over-time constantly denies Tree Dance, and Venomous Gale/Poison Nova still hit him perched or disguised -- though he punishes a caught-off-guard Venomancer hard in return.
Nethertoxin denies Jingu Mastery stacking, and his damage-over-time stops Tree Dance while ignoring Wukong's Command's armor.
Powershot destroys the tree under him, his tree-reliance is easy Shackleshot bait, and Windrun's evasion denies Jingu stacking.

His poor, rarely-built armor makes Jingu Mastery and Wukong's Command deadly, and Desolator/Sange and Yasha/Diffusal Blade all boost damage or speed to match a Chemical Rage Alchemist -- Monkey King's agility scaling also outpaces Acid Spray's late-game value.
He can scout her positioning from trees and jump in freely to disable Marksmanship, and she has no mobility to escape Wukong's Command's bonus armor advantage.

His clones from Wukong's Command/Aghanim's are immune to Chronosphere, making it a bad target while he's surrounded by them, and he can cast the ultimate right next to a Chronosphere to force Void's team to scatter.

Jingu Mastery still stacks through Guardian Angel, he can engage on his own terms directly onto Omniknight, laning-phase Jingu-boosted Boundless Strike outpaces weak early Purification, and Heavenly Grace does nothing against his ultimate or Jingu's bonuses.
He gains Jingu Mastery stacks off clone hits via Divided We Stand, and Tree Dance lets him ambush a lone clone.
Sprout doesn't protect against Tree Dance, and Boundless Strike interrupts Teleportation even reaching him inside the tree line.

His low armor discourages a trade while Jingu Mastery lets Monkey King retaliate, a buffed Boundless Strike heals him and can finish Pudge, he can scout Pudge's position from trees to dodge Meat Hook, and his above-average strength gain usually survives the combo.
Boundless Strike's long cast easily interrupts a channeling Requiem, his lack of mobility makes him easy Primal Spring ambush bait, and staying close denies all three razes before Jingu stacks up.

Dispersion does nothing against his sustained Jingu-lifesteal damage all game, a common Manta denies Desolate in 1v1, Haunt can't stop anyone trapped in his ultimate, and she's an easy early gank/pressure target.
His low mobility and lack of stuns/roots make him easy prey, silence doesn't block Jingu Mastery's damage/lifesteal, and his common Black King Bar answers the silence entirely.
Firestorm's percent damage barely dents his low HP, Jingu Mastery's benefits ignore Atrophy Aura's flat reduction, and he can get on top of Underlord easily at any stage.
His very low health lets Monkey King ambush and finish him off fast.
Paralyzing Cask's short stun rarely stops an ambush, and Death Ward's long channel is easily interrupted by Boundless Strike.

119.note: Counterspell negates her burst and can block Cursed Crown, Blink dodges a long-cast Terrorize or escapes Bramble Maze before it traps him, and her mana-hungry combo feeds a big Mana Void.
Berserker's Call forces her to attack, cancelling Shadow Realm outright.
Magnetic Field lets him or allies evade her Shadow Realm attacks, extendable with a clone, and Spark Wraith exploits her low mobility.
Quill Spray's constant AoE still hits her in Shadow Realm and punishes a Bedlam approach.
Gust reaches beyond a defensive Bramble Maze and lands before she closes for Bedlam, and her long range lets her hit the team without entering the Maze.
Flame Guard blocks her burst and punishes a Bedlam approach, and Sleight of Fist/Fire Remnant make her disable hard to land fully.

Blade Fury dispels most of her kit, passing through Bramble Maze and cancelling a pre-stun Cursed Crown -- though she can tank Omnislash safely from inside Shadow Realm since it's invulnerable to right-clicks.
An active Rage protects against and dispels her whole kit.
His burst is hard for her low health to survive long enough to escape via Shadow Realm, and walking into Bramble Maze deliberately sets up a free Spiked Carapace stun.

An undisjointable Fortune's End nearly guarantees a disable if she tries to Shadow-Realm away, and it also dispels Cursed Crown/Terrorize, Fate's Edict negates her whole magic combo, and False Promise's strong dispel clears her disables.
Her area-targeted kit still hits Willow inside Shadow Realm, Illusory Orb bypasses Bramble Maze to close and Waning Rift silence, and Phase Shift dodges a long-cast Terrorize easily.
Rot/Meat Hook both hit her even under Shadow Realm, and Flesh Heap cuts her magic burst.
Smoke Screen renders her defenseless, and Blink Strike jumps past Bramble Maze.
Last Word/Arcane Curse both outrange Bramble Maze, and Global Silence shuts her down in fights entirely.
Ball Lightning bypasses Bramble Maze into the backline and zips out again if Terrorized.
Ancient Seal instantly shuts down her whole kit while leaving her exposed to his burst, and Mystic Flare still hits her through Shadow Realm.
Bramble Maze hinders his chase-and-pick-off playstyle hard, and Shadow Realm lets her teleport away untouched.
Terrorize forces him out of a channeling Chronosphere.
Terrorize forces him out of Wukong's Command.
Bramble Maze cast right on top of him nearly guarantees a root given the clone density, and Terrorize/Cursed Crown are strong disables against a grouped swarm that denies a Poof escape.
Bramble Maze's long duration blocks an incoming Charge outright, and Shadow Realm-into-Bedlam right as Charge lands denies a Nether Strike follow-up.
Bramble Maze roots him even if he tries to Timber Chain away, Cursed Crown can still catch him mid-chain, and Reactive Armor offers little against her magic burst.
Her burst and stun keep him from approaching until he affords Black King Bar, and his lack of burst gives her plenty of time to slip into Shadow Realm.
Windrun doesn't stop Cursed Crown's stun or her magic nukes, and Focus Fire can't target her in Shadow Realm, wasting the ultimate if used too early.

12.note: Berserker's Call traps him in his own illusion crowd, and Counter Helix with Blade Mail clears the illusions fast.
His tankiness and rear damage reduction make him hard to burst without real damage, Quill Spray shreds illusions, and the passive still triggers even after a Diffusal drain.
Hoof Stomp and Double Edge clear his illusions fast, and Retaliate with Blade Mail reflects his damage right back.
Ion Shell picks off illusions to expose the real one, and Surge lets his team simply outrun the chase.
Breathe Fire/Elder Dragon splash clears illusions fast, and landing Dragon Tail on the real one can end the fight.
AoE stuns clear his illusions fast (worse with Aghanim's cleave), though Echo Slam's damage does scale hugely off the illusion count.
Sleight of Fist and Flame Guard both shred his illusions, and Fire Remnant teleports let Ember dodge Phantom Rush chases.
Stroke of Fate clears illusions in one hit, Ink Swell stuns the group, and Soulbind's undispellable mark identifies the real one and blocks Doppelganger.
Flak Cannon and Call Down both shred his illusion army fast.
Acorn Shot with an attack modifier chews through his illusions quickly, and Bushwhack stuns the whole group near a tree.
His whole AoE kit (Dual Breath, Liquid Fire, Ice Path into Macropyre) clears illusions fast, and he can predict Doppelganger with Ice Path.
Tidebringer and his other AoE abilities clear illusions efficiently.
Overwhelming Odds hits his illusions hard, and Duel's long lockout denies Doppelganger.
His untargeted AoE (Diabolic Edict, Pulse Nova) hits him regardless of which illusion is real.
Poof from multiple clones shreds illusions fast, Earthbind's root traps the group, and his early-game focus means he's simply outscaled once Phantom Lancer hits late game.
Empower helps clear illusions fast, Reverse Polarity/Skewer group him and his illusions for easy nuking, and Shockwave's early damage can even reveal the real one.
Shield Crash and the rest of his AoE kit are very effective against the illusion army.
His AoE kit chews through illusions, Fire Spirits cripples the group's attack speed, and Supernova is both immune to illusion damage and burns them down.
Illusory Orb and Waning Rift are strong early nukes against the illusions, and Dream Coil limits his mobility in fights.
Plasma Field damages or kills illusions outright, Static Link marks the real one even through Doppelganger, and Eye of the Storm plus Aghanim's shreds his armor.
His AoE kit deals with illusions well, though Epicenter alone usually isn't enough to punish a Doppelganger escape.
Multiple AoE options (more with Aghanim's) clear illusions, and Ball Lightning both destroys illusions and is hard to catch with Phantom Rush.
Great Cleave and God's Strength shred illusions in a couple of hits, and Storm Hammer's AoE stun lands on the group; his low mana also blunts a Diffusal drain.
Kraken Shell and Anchor Smash make him a poor illusion target, Ravage stuns the real one while clearing the rest, and Aghanim's Gush slows the whole group.
His all-AoE-pure-damage kit clears illusions easily, and Reactive Armor blunts most of the physical damage they deal.
Astral Step and Dissimilate clear illusions fast, Resonant Pulse both clears them and tanks his physical damage, and his mobility dodges Phantom Rush chases.

One of his hardest counters -- Arc Warden's single-target kit can't keep up with the illusion count, Flux pauses if any illusion is near, Phantom Rush closes in on Magnetic Field, and a Diffusal Blade drains his mana fast enough to starve Tempest Double.
Doppelganger dispels Sticky Napalm/Flamebreak, and the illusion crowd makes it hard to lasso the real one.
Doppelganger dispels Track, and he has no AoE to clear the illusions.
His single-target kit struggles against the illusion swarm, and his lack of mobility makes him easy Phantom Rush and mana-drain bait.
Doppelganger lets him dodge in and out of Power Cogs, and Clockwerk's low mobility makes him easy to overwhelm.
Doppelganger escapes Kinetic Field or Glimpse and dispels Thunder Strike outright, though Static Storm (especially with Aghanim's) is still a real threat.
No AoE or mobility to deal with the illusions, Doppelganger dispels Open Wounds, and a Diffusal Blade punishes his already-low mana.
He and the Spirit Bear lack mobility and get overwhelmed easily once slowed by Diffusal Blade, and Savage Roar just buys a moment before Phantom Rush catches up.
He can one-shot single illusions but there are simply too many to keep up with -- though initiating on him risks Sanity's Eclipse wiping the illusions and following into a heavy combo.
Too many illusions for Life Drain to handle, Doppelganger dodges Nether Blast or dispels Decrepify, and Diffusal Blade drains his large mana pool fast.
No sustained AoE against a constantly-respawning illusion army, and Spirit Lance reveals him and denies the Shadow Dance bonus while Phantom Rush chases down a Pounce escape.
Illusions burn through Refraction fast, and his core Diffusal Blade drains her small mana pool so she can't Meld to safety.
A well-farmed illusion army destroys Tombstone quickly, and Decay can't steal strength from illusions.
His lack of mobility and AoE makes him easy prey despite Viper Strike resisting Doppelganger, and his slows don't stop Phantom Rush -- though Nethertoxin's Break is worth watching for.
The illusion swarm burns through Gravekeeper's Cloak fast, and his lack of mobility makes him easy Phantom Rush bait.
Diffusal Blade drains his mana to deny Reincarnation until he buys Aghanim's Shard, his single-target Wraithfire Blast can't handle the illusion count, and Doppelganger disjoints it anyway.

120.note: Thirst gives constant sight and speed to run him down through his mobility, and Rupture punishes any use of Swashbuckle or Rolling Thunder, forcing an early cutoff or death mid-roll.
Retaliate procs on every Swashbuckle strike for real damage, and Stampede both dodges Rolling Thunder and negates Lucky Shot's slow.
Chronosphere's obstacle denies room to roll and wastes his ultimate's duration.
Soulbind pierces spell immunity to lock him rolling in place and anchor his victim nearby.
Split Shot still hits him mid-roll, and Stone Gaze stuns him during Rolling Thunder or forces an early exit.
Astral Imprisonment protects an ally through much of Rolling Thunder's early-level duration, and a Blink Dagger OD can time an initiation to ruin the cast.
Illusory Orb/Waning Rift catch him when he tries to disengage, and Dream Coil's long, spell-immunity-piercing leash disables half his kit and wastes a whole Rolling Thunder rolling in place.
Dark Pact clears Lucky Shot's slow/disarm, and Pounce's leash disables both Swashbuckle and Rolling Thunder while letting Slark escape a roll himself.
Charge of Darkness chases him down after an escape attempt, and Nether Strike ignores Rolling Thunder's spell immunity entirely.

Ice Shards can trap him inside his own Rolling Thunder arc, Shield Crash gets him back out, Snowball helps allies follow him though he can still counter-initiate with the roll, and Walrus Punch deals heavy damage even mid-roll.
Rolling Thunder hits him, Tempest Double, and allies right through Magnetic Field, ignores existing Flux stacks, and clears Spark Wraiths along the way.
Swashbuckle/Shield Crash quickly destroy her spiderling swarm, and Lucky Shot's disarm is huge against an Insatiable-Hunger Broodmother.

Swashbuckle's disarm during her Duel swings the fight to her opponent, Lucky Shot's 4-second duration can waste her whole Duel, and she's forced to bring allies to safely Duel him at all given the disarm -- Shield Crash also scales its damage resistance off nearby allies.

Lucky Shot disarms her, nullifying Unleash, a common Diffusal Blade burns her already-small mana pool fast, Swashbuckle's shorter cooldown outmaneuvers Rebound, and she gets stunned trying to Rebound through a Rolling Thunder.

Shield Crash's damage reduction scales off every clone present, even while rooted, stacking past 100%, and too many clones make dodging Rolling Thunder/Swashbuckle nearly impossible -- though a lone Pangolier still can't escape a full gank.

Swashbuckle plus Maelstrom or Diffusal Blade clears his illusions fast, his mobility dodges Phantom Rush, and a Phantom Rush chase just sets him up to be stunned by Rolling Thunder or hit by Shield Crash.
Swashbuckle-Rolling Thunder closes his range advantage fast, and Lucky Shot's disarm leaves him unable to fight back.
Swashbuckle burns Refraction charges fast, Lucky Shot can disrupt her mid-charge, his untargeted AoE hits her even in Meld, and his mobility shrugs off Psionic Trap's slow.
His mobility escapes a gank attempt, though Familiars can interrupt his ultimate's cast if they spot him, and Swashbuckle quickly burns Gravekeeper's Cloak charges.

121.note: Phase Shift disjoints Phantom's Embrace and wastes half of Soulbind's duration, and her mobility lets her burst Grimstroke before he can cast anything.
Disruption instantly removes Phantom's Embrace and can save allies from Soulbind, and Demonic Purge dispels Ink Swell.
Stampede lets Soulbound allies simply run away.

His backline positioning avoids most of Grimstroke's kit, the silence from Phantom's Embrace barely matters to a right-click hero, and his long range and fast projectiles destroy Phantoms attacking allies quickly.
Nether Swap breaks an ally out of Soulbind and can redistribute the shared damage onto herself instead.
Stroke of Fate scales with unit count and can instakill her with enough spiderlings nearby, and Phantom's Embrace gives vision when she flees into the trees.
Phantom's Embrace's silence interrupts a channeling Freezing Field, and her slow, fragile frame is easy Stroke of Fate/Ink Swell prey.
Soulbind ties down both Io and its tethered ally for single-target focus, and Phantom's Embrace's channel-interrupt denies a Relocate escape.
Ghost Shroud amplifies all of Grimstroke's damage, especially Ink Swell/Phantom's Embrace, and Death Pulse-sustained creeps just feed extra Stroke of Fate damage in lane.

Stroke of Fate scales harder against a big illusion army, Phantom's Embrace/Ink Swell's stun can deny a Doppelganger escape if timed right, and Soulbind can tie him to his own illusion to guarantee a kill if the real one is unclear.
His lack of an escape makes both Ink Swell and Stroke of Fate hard to dodge, and Phantom's Embrace's silence denies a saving Sunder.
His heavy ability reliance makes Phantom's Embrace's silence crippling, and he can't Return Chakram or attack the phantom during it, taking full damage and refreshing the cooldown.
