Disruption wastes seconds of a Windrun, Demonic Purge dispels it outright for 7 seconds of total defenselessness, and Disruption can save an ally from Shackleshot.
Disruption extends an ally's life against him or sets up a retreat or attack, and Demonic Purge cuts his mobility and removes Falcon Rush entirely.

8.note: Berserker's Call pierces spell immunity, shutting down a Blade Fury escape or an Omnislash, and his low health/high attack speed feeds Counter Helix hard.
Fiend's Grip pierces spell immunity, making Blade Fury useless as an escape.
A standard Chaos Bolt/Reality Rift combo kills him easily while Blade Fury is down, and Phantasm illusions tank Omnislash.
Demonic Conversion eats Omnislash damage for free, and Black Hole/Midnight Pulse deal damage that pierces Blade Fury.
Bulwark blocks most of Omnislash's physical damage and the alternating slash direction reduces it further, though Blade Fury's immunity does let him escape Arena of Blood.
Treants tank early Omnislash, Sprout traps him even mid-Blade Fury (worse with Aghanim's leash), and he simply out-farms and out-pushes Juggernaut.
Decrepify blocks Omnislash damage until he buys a Nullifier, and Nether Ward punishes his low mana hard even through Blade Fury's immunity.
Guardian Angel negates all physical damage, including Omnislash outright.
Astral Imprisonment saves targets from Omnislash, and Sanity's Eclipse punishes his low mana hard.
Fury Swipes ignores Blade Fury's immunity, and Enrage blunts Omnislash's damage.
Nearly his whole kit besides Blade Dance is easy Spell Steal fodder.
Meat Hook can hit and displace him mid-Blade Fury, and Dismember pierces the spell immunity outright.
Duel pierces spell immunity and locks him into fighting her, denying Omnislash.
No gap-closer means Sniper can kite and Headshot him from range all day, and long-range attacks snipe his Healing Ward safely.
Windrun negates Omnislash damage and outruns Blade Fury, and Focus Fire ignores the spell immunity entirely.

None of her spells pierce spell immunity, so Blade Fury dispels Cursed Crown/Bramble Maze and shuts her out, and she's fragile enough for Omnislash to end her fast (unless Shadow Realm negates the attack damage).
Blade Fury dispels her slow and burns her down early, Omnislash/Swiftslash ignore Untouchable's evasion, and Silver Edge bypasses it entirely.
Blade Fury dodges Cold Snap, Deafening Blast, Chaos Meteor and Ice Wall outright, and his damage output crushes split-pushing Forge Spirits -- though Sun Strike still hits him through Blade Fury.

Healing Ward outsustains Illuminate pressure, Blade Fury dispels Blinding Light and dodges Illuminate while still hitting towers, and his low health/armor make him easy to punish once Aghanim's Will-o-Wisp is dealt with.
Blade Fury blocks Death Pulse and Reaper's Scythe damage outright, and Ghost Shroud actually makes him take more Blade Fury damage.
Blade Fury grants immunity to everything except Vendetta, and Omnislash/Swiftslash ignore Spiked Carapace (though Vendetta can still cancel the slash).
High attack speed shreds a Supernova easily even mid-Blade Fury, and Blade Fury dodges everything else in the kit except Supernova itself.
Blade Fury's damage-over-time dispels Refraction almost instantly, and his armor lets him tank long enough to threaten Omnislash if his team can spot her.
Blade Fury blocks his entire kit, and his short range/no defenses mean he dies fast once cornered, Omnislash or not.

80.note: He and the Spirit Bear can't burst through Bristleback's damage reduction, and Viscous Nasal Goo/Quill Spray punish them both for closing in.

Poison Touch's ranged slow keeps the Spirit Bear from catching up to heal via Spirit Link, Shadow Wave/Bad Juju sustain his team through the bear's attacks, and the bear's low early armor is easy Poison Touch bait -- a common Spirit Vessel finishes the job.
He jumps in freely, separates Lone Druid from the bear to deny Spirit Link regen, and his burst usually kills Lone Druid before he even gets to use True Form.
Ghost Shroud slows or blocks the bear's attacks, and Heartstopper Aura burns the bear's high HP over time while chipping Lone Druid in True Form too.
Mystic Flare ignores the bear entirely to burst Lone Druid directly, Concussive Shot/Arcane Bolt provide vision for a better chase, and Ancient Seal denies True Form's transformation and bonus HP.

Toss separates him from the bear, giving the team a choice of target, and a Shadow Blade or Blink Dagger finds him out of True Form for an easy Avalanche-Toss kill given his tiny health pool without it.
Soulbind reliably connects to both him and the bear when they're close together.
Arcane Orb hurts both him and the bear hard, Astral Imprisonment shuts off the bear's attacking entirely, and Sanity's Eclipse deals heavy damage to Lone Druid himself.
Firestorm's percent damage demolishes the bear's high HP, and Pit of Malice lets allies kite his low mobility easily.
Cold Embrace protects allies from his and the bear's mostly-physical damage, and Winter's Curse turns them both against his own team.
Chain Frost bounces between him and the bear, forcing a costly separation.
Laser blinds him, making his attacks miss.
Bear attacks on the Supernova egg don't build hit count as fast, making the egg harder to kill given his usually-thin farm.

Acid Spray never threatens him or the bear, an entangled Alchemist wastes his Chemical Rage window, and a Monkey King Bar or Assault Cuirass Spirit Bear directly answers a Radiance Alchemist -- resummoning the bear even after it dies makes single-target focus a losing trade for Alchemist.
The bear's huge health and Spirit Link regen make Sleight of Fist nearly useless against either target, and Entangling Claws/Savage Roar deny a Fire Remnant escape entirely.
Omnislash spreads across both him and the bear so neither dies alone, and the duo's tankiness wins any early manfight.
Savage Roar interrupts Starbreaker, and his superior speed wears down a tanky but slow Dawnbreaker over time.
He's hesitant to Doom the bear, since Dooming Lone Druid instead doesn't stop the bear from still attacking, and Devour doesn't work on it while the lane push continues safely under tower.
The bear's huge health and Spirit Link regen shrug off her magic burst, and Entangling Claws roots her right as she releases Illusory Orb, denying an Ethereal Jaunt follow-up.
His huge health pool tanks a barrage of Invoker spells while killing him back, and Entangling Claws reveals a hidden Ghost Walk for the team.
His weak laning phase gets outclassed early-to-mid, Flux is nullified with the bear nearby, Spark Wraith gets soaked by the bear, and he can walk into Magnetic Field to punish Arc Warden directly.
Once the bear roots him with Entangle, he can't Teleport away.
His silence chain barely matters against a right-click-reliant hero, his poor mobility lets Lone Druid run him down, and an Aghanim's Shard clears most of Silencer's kit.

True Form's huge health pool shrugs off Ball Lightning chip damage, Entangling Claws can end him outright by denying Ball Lightning, and a common Skull Basher lets Lone Druid fear him away from either target.

81.note: Aphotic Shield punishes a Phantasm-Reality Rift combo, and Borrowed Time makes him impossible to burst down, removing a target from Chaos Knight's threat list.

A common Battle Fury clears Phantasm illusions easily, a well-timed Counterspell turns Chaos Bolt back on him, Blink dodges the slow projectile even without Counterspell up, and Mana Break drains his low mana fast -- though Anti-Mage's fragility is still a real weakness to punish.
Berserker's Call locks down him and his illusions even through Black King Bar, and Counter Helix-plus-Blade Mail clears the illusion army fast.
Storm's Dispel Magic instantly kills Phantasms early and still deals heavy damage late, revealing the real hero.
Dragon Blood's armor cuts Phantasm's damage hard, and Breathe Fire/Elder Dragon Form's splash clear illusions fast.

Echo Slam and even a low-level Fissure devastate a Phantasm army, and Aftershock's stuns always land on illusions since they lack Black King Bar -- though Earthshaker himself is easily obliterated by a farmed Chaos Knight's damage.
Untouchable slows Phantasm's physical damage hard, and Impetus deals double damage to illusions.
Black Hole usually traps him along with his whole illusion army, and Midnight Pulse's percent-health damage kills Phantasm illusions fast.
His AoE clears the Phantasm army easily, and Ice Path-into-Macropyre punishes a Chaos Knight who rarely buys Black King Bar.
Chain Frost, especially with the unlimited-bounce talent, wipes out a whole illusion army fast, and an Aghanim's Sinister Gaze hits him and his illusions while draining his already-low mana.
Reality Rift sets up a free Reverse Polarity on him and his illusions, and Shockwave, Skewer, or an Empowered melee carry all kill Phantasm illusions fast.
A Wukong's Command-Boundless Strike combo wrecks his illusion army, and without Phantasm up he has no answer to Jingu Mastery.
Purification heals a Reality Rift target while damaging him and his illusions, and Guardian Angel blocks his physical burst for a long duration.
Juxtapose overwhelms his single-target kit, a common Manta dispels or disjoints Chaos Bolt, Doppelganger dodges it outright, and a core Diffusal Blade drains his low mana pool dry.
Illusory Orb/Waning Rift clear his Phantasm army through the early-mid game, and Phase Shift disjoints Chaos Bolt.
Epicenter's massive AoE and Caustic Finale-on-death procs tear through him and his illusions fast.
Storm Hammer's fast projectile beats him to the stun before Chaos Bolt lands, Warcry's armor counters Reality Rift's shred, and Great Cleave/God's Strength devastate the illusion army.
Ravage disables him and his illusions at once, Anchor Smash's AoE hits Phantasms hard, and Kraken Shell dispels both Chaos Bolt and Reality Rift while adding protection.
Whirling Death/Chakram clear illusions fast and strip Strength from both him and his Phantasms, cutting damage and health together, while Reactive Armor stacks quickly against the illusion swarm.

Cold Embrace protects a Reality Rift target, Winter's Curse turns his own Phantasm army against him, Splinter Blast punishes the illusion count, and Arctic Burn's percent damage wears down his high max health fast.

Maledict can't be dispelled by Phantasm and tags the real hero hiding among illusions, and an Aghanim's Death Ward bounces between illusions fast -- though Chaos Bolt interrupts the ward until Witch Doctor has Glimmer Cape or Black King Bar.
His illusions make targeting the real hero with Nightmare, Enfeeble, or Fiend's Grip hard, and Chaos Bolt is a cheap, low-cooldown way to interrupt a channeling Fiend's Grip.
Phantasm dispels Track and muddies targeting the real hero, and his fragility folds fast to Chaos Knight and the illusion army.
Phantasm removes Glimpse and dispels Thunder Strike while making them hard to land on the real hero, and his lack of mobility or defense makes him easy Reality Rift bait.
Reality Rift-Chaos Bolt punishes his low armor and speed hard, he has no real AoE to clear Phantasm, and his low-health playstyle folds to Chaos Knight's burst.
The level-20 talent lets Reality Rift bypass Rage's spell immunity entirely, his lack of wave clear or lockdown struggles against the illusion army, and Chaos Strike's burst mostly ignores Feast.
Reality Rift bypasses the Spirit Bear to jump straight onto Lone Druid, and the bear's lack of scaling means it dies fast to Chaos Knight late-game.
Phantasm makes landing Meat Hook and Dismember hard, Chaos Bolt is a cheap interrupt for a channeling Dismember, and Chaos Strike's lifesteal offsets Rot's damage.

Dark Pact barely dents the illusion army since he has no other AoE, Reality Rift counteracts a Pounce escape, and his fragility folds to Chaos Knight's burst before Essence Shift stacks up -- though Shadow Dance still makes him hard to target.
His fragility and low speed make him an easy Reality Rift-Chaos Bolt target, he has no way to answer Phantasm, and his backline positioning is exactly where Chaos Knight wants to jump.
His single-target damage can't handle the illusion army, and Chaos Bolt's long stun denies his Enrage window.
His single-target focus struggles against Phantasm, and Reality Rift both counters his slows and cuts his already-poor physical durability further.

82.note: Counter Helix-plus-Berserker's Call disables multiple clones at once with heavy AoE damage, and his high survivability resists Poof/Ransack burst.
Echo Slam does catastrophic damage to a clumped clone group, and Aftershock can stun several clones at once for long enough to finish one off.

Echo Stomp disables multiple clones for 5 seconds at once, Astral Spirit treats clones as real targets for huge stat gain, and Natural Order plus Astral Spirit lets him one-shot a clone, especially punishing since Meepo tends to buy agility items.
Sleight of Fist with wave-clear items wrecks a crowded clone group fast, and Searing Chains interrupts an initiation since clones lack spell immunity.
Tidebringer's cleave wears clones down fast even in lane, Ghostship/Torrent disable while dealing heavy AoE damage, and X Marks the Spot denies a Poof escape.
A Poof-Earthbind gank into Lion's Earth Spike, or an AoE Hex talent, punishes the clone cluster hard.
Bulwark blocks attacks from Meepo and his clones, and Spear of Mars/God's Rebuke deny both initiation and escape.
Tree Dance/Primal Spring let him chase a retreating Meepo, and Boundless Strike's crit plus Wukong's Command tear through the clone swarm fast.

His wide-area kit is deadly even against Meepo's magic resistance, Shield Crash's damage reduction scales absurdly against many clones, Rolling Thunder disrupts initiation or escape, Swashbuckle hits every clone, and Lucky Shot disarms them.
Great Cleave/God's Strength tear through the clone swarm fast, and clones lack spell immunity so Storm Hammer always lands.
Reactive Tazer locks down multiple clones at once, and Proximity Mines/Sticky Bomb/Blast Off! all deal heavy AoE magic damage across the swarm.
Focus Fire instantly punishes a mis-targeted clone, Shackleshot-into-Focus Fire adds collateral damage across nearby clones, and Windrun dodges Earthbind's root entirely.
An aggressive Poof-Earthbind engage is easy Noxious Plague bait, and his constant slows cripple Meepo's mobility hard.
Viper Strike denies Ransack's lifesteal, and the clone swarm's poor magic resistance makes focused Poison Attack/Viper Strike on one clone very effective.
Winter's Curse late-game is nearly a death sentence for Meepo and any nearby clones, and landing it on just one clone bypasses a Linken's or Lotus Orb answer entirely.
Earthbind denies a Blink escape, letting Meepo finish him with attacks and Ransack.
Duelling one clone still leaves the others free to fight or help the duelled clone deal damage -- though an Aghanim's Legion Commander can stack enough duel damage to end a clone outright.
Poof quickly destroys his illusions, and Earthbind denies a Doppelganger escape.

Earthbind denies Icarus Dive, his only escape, Poof's burst kills him even through a Fire Spirits slow, the clone swarm destroys the Supernova egg fast even slowed, and Meepo's high magic resistance makes bursting him back hard while Icarus Dive is down.
A chain of Earthbinds denies her Blink, letting Meepo finish her with Poof and attacks, and his usual attribute items blunt her magic burst.
Poof destroys Disruption illusions fast and lets Meepo escape Shadow Poison/Demonic Purge quickly.
Earthbind's root, like any root, shuts off Ball Lightning entirely.

83.note: He can traverse trees just as easily, denying Treant's tree-hiding advantage.
Doppelganger dispels Leech Seed, and it destroys enough trees to counteract both Nature's Guise and Eyes in the Forest.
His whole kit is worth stealing, and Rubick casts every spell with zero cast time.
Corrosive Haze reveals him even under Nature's Guise.
All his active abilities cut down trees, and Whirling Death/Timber Chain specifically need trees to be effective, directly countering both Nature's Guise and Eyes in the Forest.
Living Armor shields against his slow, low-damage attacks entirely.
Overgrowth denies both Blink and attacking at once -- though a farmed Manta Style fully dispels it, so good Anti-Mage players save Manta for exactly that moment.
He has no teleport and relies entirely on attacking, so Overgrowth's root-and-disarm shuts him down completely.
Overgrowth shuts him down entirely except for Electric Vortex.
Her total reliance on attacks and lack of mobility make her easy prey for Overgrowth's disarm and slow.
Overgrowth denies Blink Strike even through spell immunity, and Living Armor blunts her ganking damage.

84.note: Blink kites his low mobility easily, and his intelligence-heavy build feeds a bigger Mana Void.
Phantasm dispels Ignite and muddies targeting the real hero.
Doom makes him far less disruptive, Infernal Blade punishes his durability, and an Aghanim's Doom disables Multicast.
Rage ignores his whole kit, and his big health pool feeds Feast hard.
His single-target, magic-only kit struggles to punish a clone swarm.
He has no undispellable AoE or disable for the illusion army, and Doppelganger disjoints or dispels Ignite outright.
Heavenly Grace shortens Fireblast's stun and dispels Ignite, and Purification heals through his damage.
Fate's Edict blocks his mostly-magic kit outright, and Fortune's End/False Promise dispel Ignite, Fireblast, or Bloodlust.
Dark Pact dispels both Ignite's slow and Fireblast's stun, and Shadow Dance's regen shrugs off Ignite's damage-over-time.
Viper Strike breaks Multicast, and Corrosive Skin minimizes Ignite/Fireblast's damage.
Ignite denies a Blink Dagger initiation or escape, and Fireblast can interrupt his combo follow-up right after Echo Slam lands.

Fireblast interrupts a Tether escape, and Ignite's total damage can out-trade the sustained heal Io provides its laner -- though a laner less reliant on early fights is usually the better answer overall.
Ignite or a Hand of Midas-boosted Multicast clears treants fast, and Fireblast denies a Teleportation escape.
Ignite's damage-over-time burns through Refraction's block instances, and a precast Fire Shield blunts a Meld-charged burst.

A Multicast Fireblast can deny both Shukuchi and Time Lapse, and Ignite's early damage pressures his tiny health pool hard -- though the slow itself does little against Shukuchi and Time Lapse dispels it anyway.

Multicast Fireblasts are a real nuisance against his damage output, Bloodlust/Ignite's speed lets the team chase or disengage from Warcry, Ignite pressures his health early and disrupts a Blink Dagger initiation, and his lane presence delays Sven's jungle transition -- an Aghanim's Shard even cuts his hit-based burst further.

85.note: Greevil's Greed turns Tombstone zombies into a big gold advantage.
Tombstone's zombies amplify Echo Slam's damage by adding more units to the echo.
Flak Cannon clears the zombies easily.

Moon Glaives/Lunar Blessing, worse with Manta, destroy Tombstone easily, its spell-immune zombies mean Eclipse only hits Undying himself, and Luna's natural Black King Bar lets her ignore his usual Blade Mail.
Reaper's Scythe finishes him regardless of Decay's strength gain once he's below the threshold, and Heartstopper Aura scales worse the more strength he's stolen.
Arcane Curse discourages his spammy kit with stacking damage, and Last Word/Global Silence deny both his strength steal and healing for up to 6 seconds.
His whole kit is easy Spell Steal fodder.
A maxed Kraken Shell, worse with the level-20 talent, takes almost no zombie damage, letting him just Blink away safely.
Tombstone chews through his treants for free income, and the resulting unit-heavy skirmishes buff Soul Rip further.
Tombstone's zombies have no counter in her kit, nearby Haunt illusions boost Soul Rip further, and Decay shuts her down easily in lane.
Decay steals more and more strength off his high strength gain, making Undying increasingly tanky and hard for Ogre to actually kill.
Decay's health reduction makes a Double Edge risky for him, and Tombstone attacks don't proc Retaliate since it only triggers on regular attacks.
Zombies usually outrun her, making Tombstone hard to deal with, and an ally under Cold Embrace is easy Decay bait since the damage still applies.
Decay both shrinks his max health and cuts his ultimate's damage, and Tombstone zombies plus Flesh Golem slow him enough that his slow right-click swings are wasted on the tombstone itself.
Decay makes him more vulnerable and cuts his tankiness hard.

86.note: Counterspell resists Fade Bolt and reflects most of his single-target spells, leaving only Blink useful, and Mana Break can drain him dry before he even gets a cast off.
His low damage means Bristleback just shrugs off any stolen spell and runs him down with Quill Spray/Warpath, and Rubick gains no Warpath value from casting a stolen spell instead of attacking.

His poor armor makes him easy solo gank prey, only Skeleton Walk is worth stealing, and a common Orchid denies retaliation entirely -- countering the invisibility properly eats into the ward budget for better support items.
Crippling Fear's undispellable silence shuts down his retaliation, and Hunter in the Night plus Dark Ascension find and burst him with no defensive items needed.
His low armor makes him an easy primary target, Fade Bolt alone can't burst her down, and Telekinesis is his only real answer but rarely buys enough time to escape.

His invisibility and burst let him gank and kill Rubick before a reaction, Cloak and Dagger makes his spells hard to steal outside an initiation, and countering it properly costs a lot of Sentry Wards that could go toward better items.
Dark Pact's strong dispel neuters most stolen spells, Pounce-Dark Pact-plus-attacks burst him down fast, and Shadow Dance's untargetability denies a steal window entirely.

Fade Bolt alone can't burst him, especially through Enrage, Enrage's status resistance shortens a Telekinesis lockdown, and he melts Rubick fast up close while offering nothing worth stealing since Fury Swipes is passive.
Ether Shock is a cheap farming nuke, Hex/Shackles add real lockdown to ganks, Arcane Supremacy extends their cast range for safer positioning, and Telekinesis can interrupt a channeling Shackles.
Ion Shell, Vacuum, Surge, and Wall of Replica are all worth stealing, Rubick tends to double up with Aghanim's, and Telekinesis can set enemies up inside a stolen Wall of Replica illusion field.

Chaotic Offering is devastating if stolen and dropped on a group, Telekinesis interrupts a channeling Upheaval or relocates a unit to interrupt it, and Aghanim's Shard-upgraded Telekinesis can save an ally from its slow.

Waning Rift silences and denies Phase Shift entirely, Dream Coil disables movement and items including Blink Dagger for a long time, Phase Shift itself grants Rubick invulnerability to safely reposition, and his low cast time lets Telekinesis initiate fast.

Dragon Slave/Light Strike Array are cheap steals, his fixed fast cast time makes them land easier than Lina's own, Telekinesis can throw a victim straight into a Light Strike Array for a guaranteed stun, and Laguna Blade's burst gets amplified further by Arcane Supremacy and his talent.
Stroke of Fate is a fast, cheap nuke for Rubick to farm with, Phantom's Embrace adds silence and damage, and Telekinesis extends Phantom's Embrace's latch or sets up an Ink Swell combo.
Freezing Field, once stolen, deals much more damage thanks to Arcane Supremacy, and being a channel it's easy to steal -- a well-timed Telekinesis lift or drop can even interrupt it.

Poison Nova, if stolen, hits even harder than Venomancer's own thanks to Arcane Supremacy, and Rubick can steal it from outside the cast's own effect radius while Venomancer's mana problems don't apply to him.
Shrapnel's long range pairs well with Arcane Supremacy for safe constant damage, and a stolen Assassinate with Aghanim's becomes a reliable long-range stun with massive damage.

Blade Fury, with Aghanim's Shard's speed buff, turns Rubick into a temporary tank early, and it can be stolen right back to negate Juggernaut's own cast against him -- though Omnislash falls off as a steal target since Rubick rarely scales his own physical damage.
Firestorm and Pit of Malice are both strong steals for farming and area control, and his lack of a reposition tool while stuck on the frontline makes him easy Pit of Malice bait.

Hex and Earth Spike both work identically when stolen for real lockdown, Arcane Supremacy extends their range for safer casting, and a stolen Finger of Death, empowered by Aghanim's, becomes a serious burst nuke.
Wraithfire Blast is an easy, high-value steal -- an 8, or 6 with talent, second cooldown stun locks down a hero with little mobility, and Fade Bolt negates his skeleton summons' damage.

Black Hole is devastating if stolen since Enigma has no other spell to replace it during the channel, Telekinesis or Malefice can interrupt his real Black Hole even through Black King Bar from Arcane Supremacy's extra range -- though a smart Enigma buys Linken's alongside it to deny the steal outright.

Supernova is a huge teamfight-swinging steal, Telekinesis can protect the egg right before it lands, and interrupting Icarus Dive or Sun Ray with Telekinesis denies his escape or sustain -- though sustaining Rubick's own health while doing this favors buying regen items.
Death Ward is a channeled, high-burst steal that Telekinesis can lock a target inside of, and Maledict amplifies whatever damage Rubick's team piles on next.

Requiem of Souls becomes a serious nuke once stolen, with Telekinesis able to drop a victim right on top of Rubick to eat every line of damage -- his own right-click still punishes Rubick hard in return.
Tombstone is a strong steal for counter-initiating fights and denying vision, and it's hard for Undying himself to destroy given his low attack speed.
Reverse Polarity turned against his own team punishes an over-extended initiation badly, and Telekinesis can set up his own Skewer follow-up.
Torrent and Ghostship both add real teamfight control when stolen, and Telekinesis can drop a target directly into either one.
Lucent Beam/Eclipse both become strong steals, especially amplified by Arcane Supremacy and Aghanim's upgrades.

Attribute Shift (Strength) permanently reshapes Rubick's stats for more tankiness even after losing the spell, and a stolen Adaptive Strike (Strength) is a long-range stun that punishes mobile heroes.

87.note: Aphotic Shield dispels Thunder Strike, Mist Coil heals an ally trapped in Static Storm-Kinetic Field, and Borrowed Time makes him nearly ungankable.

Void's damage and slow plus Crippling Fear's silence overwhelm his no-escape kit, and Hunter in the Night's speed lets Night Stalker close and finish him -- a common Black King Bar all but guarantees the kill.
Blade Fury moves him straight out of Kinetic Field and dodges Glimpse entirely, Healing Ward sustains anyone trapped in Static Storm, and Omnislash dodges Glimpse too.
Rage escapes a Glimpse pull and moves him out of Kinetic Field, and Infest dodges Glimpse outright.
Purification sustains an ally trapped in Static Storm, and Repel grants reliable immunity to it.
Doppelganger reliably dodges Glimpse and escapes Kinetic Field so long as Static Storm isn't already down.
Nether Ward punishes his high mana costs hard, and Life Drain heals an ally caught in the Static Storm-Kinetic Field combo if Pugna isn't the target.
His range lets him kill Disruptor from outside Kinetic Field's reach, and he plays too far back for Disruptor to easily land spells in lane.
Corrosive Skin minimizes damage from his entire kit.
Glimpse disables Blink just like it does Queen of Pain, cutting his mobility -- though Counterspell blocks most of the damage, usually requiring a partner to finish the kill.

Glimpse pulls Io or its tethered ally right back after a Relocate, and pre-dropping Static Storm/Kinetic Field on the visible relocate marker punishes the escape before it lands; Thunder Strike/Glimpse also recover an ally Tethered away in the fog.
Glimpse heavily counters her Blink-and-positioning playstyle, and Static Storm devastates a hero who relies on burst spell damage.

Thunder Strike gives vision on him through invisibility, a level 3-4 Glimpse pulls him back into a favorable fight, jumping Disruptor means stepping into his own Kinetic Field, and the AoE silence, even muting Black King Bar, is deadly to Slark at every stage.

By roughly the 10-minute mark a leveled Glimpse can pull him back to a Static Storm even after a Ball Lightning escape given his limited mana at that point -- though late-game he can often kill first and let Glimpse simply return him to safety afterward.

None of Disruptor's spells are dispellable, making it easy to trap him in Kinetic Field or Static Storm even though Kraken Shell keeps him tanky enough to need real follow-up, and a high-level Glimpse cancels a Ravage channel or a Town Portal before Linken's or Black King Bar comes online -- though Static Storm's silence works around a reactive Linken's anyway.

88.note: Berserker's Call exposes him mid-Vendetta and denies Spiked Carapace, Battle Hunger's damage-over-time weakens the Carapace reflection, and his high health, often into Heart of Tarrasque, shrugs off Nyx's burst while Culling Blade finishes a fragile Nyx once Carapace is down.
Track hinders his Vendetta ganks and escapes for a bounty, and it deals no damage so it can even be cast on him mid-Spiked Carapace safely.
Blood Rite punishes a burrowed Nyx unless Spiked Carapace is timed perfectly, and Thirst/Rupture both deny a Vendetta escape.
Cyclone's duration outlasts Spiked Carapace, wasting it entirely.
A well-timed Doom denies both a Vendetta escape and a Spiked Carapace counter, and his high health shrugs off Nyx's burst.
Blade Fury and Omnislash/Swiftslash both grant immunity that Spiked Carapace can't punish, and Healing Ward sustains through his damage -- any Nyx gank on Juggernaut usually backfires.

Rage grants immunity just like Blade Fury does, Aghanim's Open Wounds/Infest slow and disarm him from within, immune to Spiked Carapace the same way, and any gank attempt tends to hurt Nyx more than Lifestealer.
Lucent Beam punishes him hard whenever Spiked Carapace is down, her natural Black King Bar lets her attack through it freely, and Dust of Appearance denies a Vendetta pick-off.
His high health shrugs off Nyx's burst, his natural Black King Bar lets him attack freely through Spiked Carapace, and his wolves can hit Nyx safely while it's active.
Corrosive Haze hinders a Vendetta gank while cutting his armor, and Guardian Sprint's speed finishes him off with vision.
Corrosive Skin minimizes his whole burst kit, and stacked poison damage overwhelms him even through Spiked Carapace since he rarely buys the Silver Edge that would help.

Familiars deal many small hits that outlast Spiked Carapace's window, Gravekeeper's Cloak plus tanky items resist his burst, and an Aghanim's Stone Form both heals Visage and stuns Nyx if he's nearby.
Spiked Carapace interrupts Freezing Field easily, Frostbite's damage-over-time sets up an easy stun, and her fragility folds fast to his burst.
Spiked Carapace interrupts Starbreaker, before her Aghanim's, and the initial Solar Guardian channel, and Celestial Hammer's slow projectile makes her easy to stun while engaging or chasing.
Spiked Carapace reflects Impetus, and her squishiness folds fast to his burst.
Malefice/Midnight Pulse's uncontrolled damage set up easy Spiked Carapace stuns, and Impale/Carapace both interrupt a channeling Black Hole.
Flame Guard or a Battle Fury easily triggers Spiked Carapace, setting up a deadly Impale.

Split Shot's passive attacks and Mystic Snake's uncontrolled damage both trigger Spiked Carapace, Mana Burn shreds Mana Shield fast, worse if she stacks intelligence, and her lack of single-target damage makes a burrowed Nyx hard to kill.

His high intelligence and fragility make him easy Mana Burn and burst prey, an un-targeted Astral Imprisonment sets up a free stun either way, and Spiked Carapace punishes a Sanity's Eclipse attempt unless he's got Black King Bar first.
Spiked Carapace triggers off any of his damage-over-time abilities and can interrupt Sun Ray or Icarus Dive.

Illusory Orb reflects easily off Spiked Carapace for a stun setup, her intelligence-item build is Mana Burn bait, an ill-timed Phase Shift still leaves her open to Impale, and her low armor and agility make her a natural Vendetta target.
Nether Blast's animation makes Spiked Carapace easy to time, his huge intelligence gain is prime Mana Burn bait, and a channeling Life Drain is easy Impale bait.

Last Word reflects hard off Spiked Carapace while still landing its silence, Glaives of Wisdom builds his intelligence into a bigger Mana Burn target, and he rarely builds survivability or has team cover to deny an easy Vendetta.
Assassinate reflects easily off Spiked Carapace, Shrapnel's AoE sets up a stun especially paired with Vendetta, and his low early health and high intelligence make him easy prey.
Mana Burn removes the mana Ball Lightning needs, and Static Remnant triggers Spiked Carapace for an easy stun.
Heat-Seeking Missile sets up easy Spiked Carapace stuns, his mana-and-intelligence-item reliance is prime Mana Burn bait, and Nyx's stuns interrupt Rearm to leave him helpless.

89.note: He procs Counter Helix more often being hit by an illusion swarm, destroying them fast.
Stacked Sticky Napalm plus Flamebreak/Firefly clears her illusions, letting him Flaming Lasso the real one and drag her away from a Song of the Siren escape.

Starbreaker/Celestial Hammer/Solar Guardian all clear illusion waves fast, an Aghanim's Starbreaker dispels Ensnare to attack freely through Song of the Siren, and Solar Guardian counters her split-push or ambushes her after a Song of the Siren.
An Aghanim's Poison Touch instantly destroys her whole illusion set.

Moon Glaives/Lunar Blessing, worse with Gleipnir/Manta, clear her illusions fast, letting Eclipse finish her before Song of the Siren, an Aghanim's ministun Eclipse repeatedly stuns and denies the escape at range, and Luna's natural Black King Bar lets her ignore Song of the Siren entirely while Naga rarely buys one back.
His strong AoE clears illusions or at least reveals the real one by the extra damage they take, and Echo Slam scales devastatingly against a whole illusion set.
His damage-over-time clears illusions and still hurts the real Naga through Song of the Siren, and she rarely buys the Black King Bar that would help.

Blade Fury clears illusions and can hit the real Naga if she hides among them, an Aghanim's Blade Fury with the DPS talent shreds the whole set almost instantly, and Diffusal Blade does nothing to a spell-immune Juggernaut.
Hex/Mana Drain instantly destroy illusions, worse with the AoE Hex talent or Shard Mana Drain, crippling her push, and Earth Spike's AoE damage helps distinguish the real Naga by the damage taken.

Split Shot/Mystic Snake with a common Mjollnir whittle down her whole illusion set including herself, and Stone Gaze locks her down even through spell immunity, discouraging a Song of the Siren counter-initiate.
Waveform clears her illusions, Ensnare can be dispelled with a common Manta, and an Aghanim's Morph can copy her kit to make a strong illusion of Naga herself while closing the gap.

Arcane Orb's pure damage bypasses her armor to clear illusions fast, Astral Imprisonment denies mana and a Song of the Siren escape, and Sanity's Eclipse can one-shot her and the illusion set while its mana-allergy debuff punishes any further casting.

Reactive Armor resists her mostly-sustained damage unless she's built as a nuker, his low-cooldown AoE, worse with Aghanim's Chakram/Flamethrower, clears illusions fast, and a common Lotus Orb reflects Ensnare back at her.
His burst ignores her high armor, Arc Lightning bounces to clear illusions, and an Aghanim's Static Field auto-hits her whole illusion set regardless of their health.
Flak Cannon/Call Down easily clear her illusions.
Mortimer Kisses and Scatterblast/Firesnap Cookie's AoE make quick work of her illusions.
His AoE, especially Pulse Nova, tears through her illusions easily, and an Aghanim's Nihilism slows and exposes her and her illusions to magic damage while he moves freely.
Retaliate exposes the real Naga among attackers, and a Hoof Stomp-into-Double Edge clears the illusion set while denying a Song of the Siren escape.

Atrophy Aura makes it hard to farm or fight without a nuker build, Firestorm clears her illusions fast, though Song of the Siren can still ambush an unprepared Fiend's Gate arrival or Ensnare/Reel In can deny the escape.

Song of the Siren wastes his Borrowed Time entirely while keeping him in place, Mirror Image dispels Curse of Avernus before the fourth stack lands, and a Heart of Tarrasque both survives Aphotic Shield's illusion-clearing and makes her harder to pick out.
Song of the Siren stops him cold to let her team close the gap past Magnetic Field, Mirror Image dispels or resists Flux's slow, and her illusions compete directly with his split-push game.
His single-target kit struggles against her illusions, Mirror Image dispels a landed Track, and Ensnare reveals him through invisibility while rooted.

Mirror Image dispels Frostbite, Song of the Siren stops a Freezing Field channel regardless of invisibility while closing the gap, Ensnare lets the team catch up fast, and an Aghanim's Reel In cancels Freezing Field even through Black King Bar.

Her illusions make his combo hard to land, Rip Tide hurts him and clears his creeps, Ensnare denies his escape, and an Aghanim's Reel In separates him from his army entirely since he has no way to cancel it.
Song of the Siren's duration is long enough to deny a successful Duel outright, as long as Naga isn't the target.
Without a Black King Bar on the bear, Ensnare kites it easily, Song of the Siren lets her team bypass the bear and hunt Lone Druid directly, and her illusions face no AoE answer from his kit.
His single-target, no-AoE kit has no answer to her illusions or Ensnare.
Rip Tide out-pushes and out-farms his treants, and Ensnare denies Teleportation even from inside Sprout since Song of the Siren outlasts the hiding time.
Mirror Image can bait a wasted Void since he can't tell which illusion is real -- though his own Aghanim's Void can still hit and locate the real Naga in fights.

Song of the Siren wastes Guardian Angel entirely, Ensnare still lands through Heavenly Grace since only a dispel removes it, and her natural Diffusal Blade plus magic-damage items punish a Guardian-Angel-protected target.
Song of the Siren doesn't stop Supernova, letting her team focus the egg during the sleep, and Ensnare denies an Icarus Dive escape -- though his AoE spells still clear her illusions.

Song of the Siren is hard for him to Spell Steal while asleep, Ensnare-Rip Tide-plus-attacks burst his low health and armor fast, a natural Diffusal Blade drains his mana, and Mirror Image dodges a Telekinesis stun or dispels a landed Fade Bolt.
Ensnare-plus-attacks makes ganking him trivial, and Rip Tide strips his already-thin armor.
Ensnare disables both her invisibility and a core Blink Dagger, and the illusion swarm breaks Refraction fast.

Mirror Image easily dispels Reflection, his only real tool to spot the real Naga, worsened by Conjure Image's different-colored illusions, an Aghanim's Ensnare/Reel In pulls him away from his own illusions even through Black King Bar, Rip Tide punishes his low strength hard, and Song of the Siren buys time to undo a Sunder -- though her weak burst can struggle to close out the kill without Black King Bar or Linken's.

Mirror Image dispels Corrosive Skin, his single-target kit has almost no answer to her illusions, and his lack of burst gives her plenty of time to Song of the Siren a save, Aghanim's even healing allies through it.

9.note: Aphotic Shield or Borrowed Time strip Sacred Arrow's stun instantly, making her Aghanim's combo very hard to land.
Flux still lands after a Leap, and Magnetic Field can protect an ally who got hit by Sacred Arrow.
Rupture punishes a Leap escape, and Thirst spots her and allies during Moonlight Shadow.
Track spots her and allies through Moonlight Shadow invisibility.
Her spiderling swarm and web speed make her hard to land Sacred Arrow on, and a well-itemized Broodmother can shut down both her escapes and Starstorm.
Eul's plus Light Strike Array denies a Leap escape, and Laguna Blade's burst punishes her low health.
Her speed dodges Sacred Arrow, and a well-itemized Luna can spot her through Moonlight Shadow and punish with Aghanim's Eclipse.
Shapeshift dodges Sacred Arrow and outruns a Leap escape.
Earthbind denies both Leap and Moonlight Shadow, and hitting one clone with Sacred Arrow leaves the rest free to fight.
The long night-time Crippling Fear denies both her escapes, and his tankiness plus Dark Ascension/Gem let him hunt her down at any stage.
Waning Rift denies her escapes, Dream Coil punishes a Leap attempt, and Phase Shift dodges Sacred Arrow/Starstorm entirely while his burst punishes her low health.
Dark Pact can remove an incoming Sacred Arrow, Pounce denies Leap, and Shadow Dance lets him survive her Aghanim's combo.
Windrun dodges Sacred Arrow, and a Shackleshot-into-Aghanim's-Focus-Fire combo can kill her before she escapes.
Rod of Atos/Gleipnir land Sacred Arrow through his usual Manta cooldown, Leap outruns him, and Moonlight Shadow lets her simply vanish from the fight.
Sacred Arrow interrupts Freezing Field from a safe distance, her terrible mobility makes her easy arrow bait, and Leap still escapes even through Crystal Nova/Freezing Field's slow.
Leap or Moonlight Shadow gets Mirana in range without eating Marksmanship's bonus, her low health folds to Mirana's Aghanim's combo, and Gust/slows are dodgeable with good reactions.
Techies spends a lot of time standing still planting mines -- Sacred Arrow scouts and can catch him before Blast Off, and her attack range clears traps safely.
Leap easily outruns a thrown Snowball.
Sacred Arrow interrupts Death Ward from a safe distance, Leap dodges a slow-moving Paralyzing Cask, and his low health folds fast to her Aghanim's combo.

90.note: Nether Blast wins the lane push outright, and Nether Ward denies farming Illuminate off creeps.
Blade Fury grants immunity to his whole kit, and Healing Ward sustains through his weak magic burst.
Press the Attack dispels Blinding Light/Solar Bind, and Duel removes him from a fight instantly.
Rage grants immunity to his whole kit, and Ghoul Frenzy's speed plus slow lets Lifestealer run him down fast given his squishiness.
Crippling Fear shuts off his whole team-sustaining kit, and Dark Ascension lets Night Stalker jump the backline and kill him fast, worse combined with Void's slow.
Spiked Carapace reflects Illuminate and stuns him, Vendetta lets Nyx chase down a split-pushing Keeper, and his squishiness folds fast to the follow-up.
Blood Rite forces a choice between finishing Illuminate's channel or eating a long silence, and Rupture completely negates his speed-based mobility.

Being entirely cast-reliant, his whole kit suffers under Silencer's -- Global Silence alone is nearly a death sentence in a fight, and Arcane Curse/Last Word punish any caster hard, though a smart Keeper buys Eul's, and later the dispel talent, to answer it.

His high mana pool and low health and armor make him ideal Mana Void bait, Counterspell resists Illuminate/Solar Bind's magic-resistance reduction and can reflect Solar Bind if timed right, and Blink dodges both spells outright -- though a careful Keeper who keeps his team's mana topped denies Mana Void entirely, and a common Octarine Core keeps his own mana full.
Illuminate's long range wins the lane outright since Viper can't fight back at that distance.
Blinding Light knocks him out of Wukong's Command and blinds him, and Will-o-Wisp destroys the tree under Tree Dance for a stun.
Illuminate wipes her spiderling swarm and denies her push while revealing her hiding spot in the trees.

91.note: Ice Blast blocks Tether healing outright, and Chilling Touch's range plus Ice Vortex's slow, worse with Aghanim's, make escaping Cold Feet nearly impossible.
Flaming Lasso cancels a Relocate escape and drags him from his tethered ally, and since Io rarely buys the Linken's that would help, an Aghanim's double-drag is a real threat.
Thirst reveals a low-health Relocate target, and Rupture locks him in place, denying Tether's speed as an escape.
Quill Spray punishes his low armor hard since he has to stay close to his tethered ally to keep the buff up.
His true-strike burst kills Io's low armor fast, and he commonly carries Orchid/Bloodthorn or Gleipnir to root and silence Io out of both Tether and Relocate.

Poison Touch harasses both Io and its tethered ally in lane, worse with Aghanim's hex locking down the pair, and since Io deals little damage, Dazzle always has time to Shadow Wave or Shallow Grave a save.
Glimpse directly negates Relocate, Kinetic Field denies a Tether escape, and Static Storm, muting both with Aghanim's, silences and damages the pair at once.
Soulbind easily catches Io and its tethered ally together given how often they stick close, and Phantom's Embrace punishes a hero this vulnerable to disables.
Homing Missile cancels a Relocate escape, and Flak Cannon/Rocket Barrage/Call Down all hit both Io and its tethered target hard.
His AoE hits both Io and its tethered ally together, Ice Path cancels both Tether and Relocate, and a common Rod of Atos denies the escape further.
Duel is brutally effective against his low health and armor.
His AoE punishes Io for needing to stay close to its tethered target, and Lightning Storm/Diabolic Edict/Pulse Nova all hit both at once.
Chain Frost forces a choice between keeping Tether up and taking devastating bounce damage, and Sinister Gaze locks him down before he can Tether or Relocate away.
Lucent Beam cancels Tether or Relocate, and Moon Glaives/Eclipse, worse with Aghanim's, make short work of Io and its tethered ally together.

Ensnare/Song of the Siren both cancel Tether/Relocate while closing distance, Rip Tide plus Mirror Image illusions can finish him off, and an Aghanim's Reel In pulls him in exactly like a Flaming Lasso -- though her weak AoE struggles against nothing Io himself provides.
Phantom Strike jumps straight to him, and Coup de Grace makes short work of his low health and armor.
Take Aim/Assassinate reach him even sitting in the backline.
Charge of Darkness both escapes and counter-initiates a Relocate gank, and Greater Bash/Nether Strike's damage plus knockback can separate him from his tethered ally.

Reflection and Metamorphosis punish his weak durability, Reflection specifically damages and slows both Io and its tethered ally through Overcharge, and his low damage output gives Terrorblade plenty of time to Sunder -- though only an Aghanim's Terror Wave actually stops Io or the pair from escaping.

Living Armor/Leech Seed can save a gank target, Overgrowth cancels a Relocate escape, and an Aghanim's Eyes in the Forest gives vision that alerts allies to an Io gank and even lets Overgrowth hit them from range.
Cold Embrace nullifies Overcharge's attack-speed bonus, and Splinter Blast/Winter's Curse both punish Io for having to stay close to its tethered target.
Her lack of an escape makes her an easy Relocate gank target.
Tether escapes Earthbind even through Blink Dagger, and Io's Spirits pressure the lane, usually hitting at least one clone.
Relocate makes ganking a split-pushing Nature's Prophet trivial, and a tethered ally can destroy his Sprout trees from inside.
His limited, damage-over-time-heavy kit gives Io plenty of time to Relocate allies to safety.
Tether/Overcharge make landing Meat Hook much harder, and Relocate saves an ally mid-Dismember channel.
Tether or Relocate escapes Pit of Malice, and Relocate directly counters a Dark Rift split-push.

92.note: Berserker's Call into his Familiar flock feeds heavy Counter Helix procs, and their fast, close-range attacks proc it constantly too.
Retaliate makes attacking him a losing trade for the Familiars, slowly killing them off.
Scorched Earth chips Gravekeeper's Cloak while engaging, Infernal Blade scales huge off his high health, and Doom fully nullifies Gravekeeper's Cloak while blocking his spellcasting.
Moon Glaives destroys Familiars fast and strips a Gravekeeper's Cloak layer on every hit, letting Eclipse finish him once both are gone.
Familiars can't damage the Supernova egg, and Sun Ray only starts burning through Gravekeeper's Cloak once it's dealt enough total damage.
Sand Storm and Epicenter both whittle Familiars down fast.
Kraken Shell blocks nearly all Familiar damage even through Medallion/Solar Crest, and Anchor Smash's bonus damage can outright kill them.
Familiar attacks stack Reactive Armor fast, and his low mobility makes lining up abilities on Visage easy.
Avalanche strips several Gravekeeper's Cloak layers at once, an Avalanche-Toss combo burns through the rest while tripling Toss damage, and Tree Grab's attack modifier shreds Familiars fast.
His damage-over-time chips Gravekeeper's Cloak while slowing an already-sluggish Visage, and even normal attacks apply Poison Sting to the same effect.
His slow speed makes kiting easy with Poison Attack/Viper Strike while chipping Gravekeeper's Cloak, Nethertoxin strips every layer instantly, and Corrosive Skin resists Soul Assumption hard.
Familiars scout his position to dodge or block Hookshot, and Gravekeeper's Cloak absorbs a big chunk of its damage.
He has no way to deal with Gravekeeper's Cloak or Familiars, whose low attack time chips his health, whose Stone Form destroys Sprout's trees, and which scout foggy areas for a Teleportation escape.
Stone Form's long stun can deny an escape entirely, and Visage commonly carries a rooting Rod of Atos or a disabling Bloodthorn to lock her down and make her more vulnerable.
His melee range and low attack speed make killing Familiars slow going, and Stone Form quickly interrupts a Dismember.
Familiars' high attack speed destroys Mass Serpent Ward fast for a big gold bounty.
Familiars chase her through the trees during a Spectral Dagger escape while Soul Assumption keeps hitting her, and Desolate rarely procs since a Familiar is usually nearby.
Familiars fly safely over mines and can scout the field, while Techies' low attack speed and damage struggles to kill them back, especially under Grave Chill.

93.note: Ice Blast stops Shadow Dance's passive regen even out of vision.
Phantom's Embrace and Soulbind both resist Dark Pact's dispel, punishing him directly or through a tethered ally.
Berserker's Call forces him to attack even mid-Shadow Dance, Counter Helix procs off his Essence Shift attack speed, and Culling Blade finishes him before he can slip away to regen.
Thirst reveals him below its threshold even during Shadow Dance, and Rupture cripples the mobility he relies on to hit-and-run.
Phantasm illusions have too much health for Dark Pact to handle, and he has no other AoE for the army.
Static Storm and Kinetic Field lock him down since Dark Pact can't dispel them, and Glimpse both stops a gank and negates a Pounce escape.
His many AoE stuns lock Slark down and often waste Shadow Dance's duration, and a common Force Staff lets him save teammates from a Pounce later.
Earthbind and Poof still hit him in Shadow Dance, Dark Pact only clears one Earthbind at a time, and Ransack still lands even through Black King Bar.
His reliance on Pounce and close range makes him easy Purification/Hammer of Purity bait, and Guardian Angel plus healing negates even a heavily stacked Essence Shift.
Arcane Orb's pure damage ignores his agility-stack armor, Astral Imprisonment can banish either him or his leashed target to disrupt Pounce, and his low mana pool feeds a big Sanity's Eclipse.

He has no sustained AoE for the illusion army, Doppelganger dodges Dark Pact/Pounce and wastes part of Shadow Dance, Spirit Lance's illusion gives vision to deny his juke, and Phantom Rush chases him down after a Pounce.
Illusory Orb/Phase Shift dodge most ganks, Waning Rift/Dream Coil make escaping very hard, and her combo's untargeted magic damage can't be avoided by Shadow Dance.
Nether Blast still hits him hidden in Shadow Dance, a defensive Decrepify on an ally denies Essence Shift stacks, and Life Drain damages and reveals him despite Pounce's ability to break it.
Sonic Wave/Scream of Pain both hit him even during Shadow Dance.
Toss/Avalanche deal heavy early damage making him a dangerous gank target, and his zero agility makes Essence Shift's permanent steal nearly worthless.
Dark Pact dispels Flux, Pounce dodges Spark Wraiths, and a split-pushing Tempest Double is easy Essence Shift fodder.
Shadow Dance's passive warns him when he's spotted, making a Flaming Lasso hard to land, and Dark Pact, or Depth Shroud with Aghanim's, dispels or prevents it entirely.

Pounce plus a Shadow Blade closes the gap she needs to keep for Marksmanship, Gust alone rarely buys enough time since she has no mobility of her own, and Essence Shift's agility drain weakens her hard.
Essence Shift pierces Blade Fury's spell immunity to steal stats regardless, Pounce escapes with nothing he can do to chase, and Shadow Dance denies Omnislash entirely while he heals and hits freely.
Her lack of mobility and escape makes her easy gank prey, and Shadow Dance dodges Eclipse's damage outright.

She has no way to chase or disable him beyond her ultimate, letting him escape, regen, and return to finish her off, and Essence Shift's intelligence drain shrinks her mana pool hard over a long fight.

Pounce closes the gap and denies a Phantom Strike escape, his natural Silver Edge strips Blur/Coup de Grace, her crit-reliant playstyle gives him plenty of time to disengage with Pounce-Shadow Dance-Silver Edge, and Essence Shift hurts her doubly by cutting both her damage and her crits -- an Aghanim's Depth Shroud even lets him save allies from her while fighting back freely.
His total lack of mobility or escape makes him easy gank prey.

Essence Shift's flat strength drain can't be reduced by Dispersion, Pounce denies a Spectral Dagger escape, and he commonly buys a Shadow Blade to dodge Haunt illusions and Desolate/Radiance while regenerating through Shadow Dance -- his natural Silver Edge also breaks both Desolate and Dispersion.
Pounce's leash denies a Ball Lightning escape, and Dark Pact dispels Orchid's Soul Burn silence.
Dark Pact tears through Refraction charges while still stealing stats, and Pounce/Dark Pact both land easily on an immobile, Melded target.
Upheaval barely interrupts him since he can just Pounce out, and Dark Pact dispels Fatal Bonds/Shadow Word.
Pounce catches her even mid-Windrun, Shadow Dance dodges Focus Fire entirely while he regens and returns, and Dark Pact dispels Shackleshot's stun or Powershot's slow if timed right.
He's one of the few heroes who can trade blows with Kez directly, escaping via Shadow Dance while Pounce negates Kez's mobility.

94.note: Mana Break burns her mana fast, worse with a common Manta drain, Blink lets him initiate and force an early Stone Gaze, and Mana Void punishes her big mana pool while threatening allies near her Mana Shield.

Either Flux bypasses Linken's Sphere, and combined with Spark Wraith slows her already-poor speed to a crawl, while a double Hand of Midas farming advantage plus duplicated items lets him bully her hard.
Culling Blade's instant-kill threshold punishes her low HP badly, making it hard for her to farm through his constant harassment.
Fiend's Grip both damages and drains mana, leaving her defenseless.
Spin Web lets her pick fights and ambush Medusa freely, and her spiderling swarm simply outnumbers what Split Shot/Mystic Snake can handle.
EMP's mana burn chips into Mana Shield hard, Deafening Blast disarms her pseudo-AoE, and Cold Snap's repeated stuns deny her long-cast ultimate.
Will-o-Wisp keeps her locked down after a Blinding Light hit.

Vendetta's burn drains her mana pool fast, Split Shot/Mystic Snake's passive damage can proc Spiked Carapace if he's in range and visible, and her lack of single-target damage makes an Aghanim's Nyx very hard for her to deal with as a main damage source.
A core Diffusal Blade burns her mana fast, weakening Mana Shield, Doppelganger's invulnerability dodges Stone Gaze or Mystic Snake, and his illusion army outnumbers her Split Shot targets.
Static Link neuters her main damage output unless she's bought Linken's, Plasma Field slows her already-poor speed to a crawl, and Eye of the Storm punishes her low armor even through Mana Shield.
Smoke Screen's silence and high miss chance flush her out of position easily, and Cloak and Dagger's backstab bonus hits hard even through Mana Shield.

Essence Shift is devastating since her strength and intelligence both feed effective HP while agility feeds damage, and a well-timed Dark Pact dispels Stone Gaze's petrify to keep attacking through the duration.
His range outranges both her arrows and Stone Gaze, letting him focus her freely in fights.
Enrage's status resistance shortens Stone Gaze's duration, and Fury Swipes stacks damage fast against Mana Shield in a long fight.
Bulwark redirects her attacks onto him, Spear of Mars stuns and displaces her given her poor mobility, and Arena of Blood blocks her ranged attacks from outside it.
Burning Spear's damage-over-time drains both her mana and health, and Inner Fire's slow and disarm sets up a Life Break follow-up.
Her small neutral-creep army feeds a late Mystic Snake bounce for easy damage.
His low mobility makes him easy to kite, and Stone Gaze pierces Rage, wasting its cooldown and leaving him unable to fight.

A Manta Style Luna feeds Split Shot/Mjollnir kills, Mystic Snake harasses and drains her mana to deny Lucent Beam retaliation, Mana Shield survives Eclipse since Luna rarely carries Diffusal Blade, and Stone Gaze disables her even through Black King Bar.
Split Shot/Mystic Snake with a common Mjollnir whittle down her whole illusion set, and Stone Gaze disables her even through spell immunity, discouraging a Song of the Siren counter.
Mana Shield tanks most of Reaper's Scythe's damage, dropping the kill threshold, and his matching speed makes him easy to kite with a slow item.
Stone Gaze lets her kite and kill him easily, and Mana Shield negates much of his burst.
Split Shot destroys Tombstone and its zombies while still damaging heroes.
His speed doesn't save him from being petrified, and his wolves feed Split Shot/Mystic Snake damage.
Split Shot makes quick, high-bounty work of his Eidolons, and Stone Gaze cancels a channeling Black Hole even through spell immunity, discouraging the initiation.
Poof doesn't damage her, and Stone Gaze disables the whole clone swarm at once, while Mystic Snake is brutal against him early.
Mana Shield blunts Counter Helix's return damage, and Stone Gaze makes it very hard for him to initiate on her or her team.
Familiars die fast to Split Shot, and Mana Shield resists Soul Assumption's damage without much effort.

95.note: Fervor/Battle Trance's attack speed feeds heavy Counter Helix procs against his low max health, a common Blade Mail turns his burst against him with Call's bonus armor amplifying it, and Culling Blade can still finish him mid-Battle-Trance if his HP is low enough.
Nightmare/Fiend's Grip both lock him down hard in fights.
Long disables waste Battle Trance's duration while kiting him, and Mass Serpent Ward traps him inside since he can't attack the wards or Phase Boots away during Trance.
His tanky illusions exploit Troll's lack of AoE, Chaos Bolt's long stun plus Reality Rift deny a chase, and a full Phantasm can kill him before Battle Trance or Black King Bar comes up.
Frostbite disarms and roots him without Black King Bar or Manta, and Freezing Field's AoE damage can't be cancelled by Troll at all while its slow sets up a gank.
Frost Blast/Chain Frost kite him effectively, and Frost Shield alone can waste most of a Battle Trance since he can't switch targets mid-Trance and has no regen to outlast it.

Fate's Edict's disarm renders him useless especially after a Battle Trance is spent, Fortune's End/Purifying Flames burst him down early-mid, and False Promise saves his target, forcing a wasted switch or Trance.

Arcane Orb's pure damage kills him fast, Astral Imprisonment removes him for 4 seconds -- potentially wasting over half a Battle Trance -- and his 1-intelligence-per-level growth makes Sanity's Eclipse often instantly lethal.
Static Link drains most or all his damage with no way to cancel the link during Battle Trance, and Storm Surge lets Razor freely chase or flee while dealing Eye of the Storm damage.
Shrapnel/Headshot kite him effectively, and Take Aim plus a Hurricane Pike lets Sniper fire from a totally safe distance.
Timber Chain kites him extremely well, Whirling Death/Chakram deal heavy damage, and Reactive Armor makes Timbersaw shrug off his attack speed even during Battle Trance.
Atrophy Aura cuts his damage, Pit of Malice locks him down, and Battle Trance can't dispel him out of either Firestorm or the Pit.
Cold Embrace protects his target especially during Battle Trance, and Winter's Curse turns his high attack speed and damage against his own team.

Whirling Axes (Melee)'s 60% miss chance denies Mana Break, the passive root fights him well and pairs devastatingly with Skull Basher/Abyssal Blade, Counterspell does nothing against physical damage, and his terrible intelligence makes him a poor Mana Void target.
Fervor/Battle Trance easily outpace Untouchable's attack-speed slow, and he naturally carries Silver Edge to disable it outright.
Whirling Axes (Melee)'s miss chance denies a lot of his attacks, and Fervor's ramp-up matches Berserker's Blood's regen scaling so Troll's attack speed eventually outpaces it.
His ranged attacks destroy Healing Ward from a distance, and Battle Trance activated during Omnislash lets him survive the whole duration and retaliate after.
Berserker's Rage's passive armor resists Feast early, Whirling Axes' miss chance helps when Rage is down, and Battle Trance purges Open Wounds to deny a big chunk of his sustain.
A Silver Edge or Monkey King Bar fully ignores Blur, Whirling Axes' miss chance makes landing Coup de Grace hard, and Battle Trance negates a crit outright.
Fervor and Battle Trance make him one of the best heroes at dealing with Supernova.

Berserker's Rage's high root chance plus attack speed lets him man-fight Sven, and Whirling Axes' miss chance plus the passive armor resist his physical damage, blunting God's Strength -- though Sven can out-farm him with Great Cleave on ancients.

Whirling Axes' miss chance plus Fervor's attack speed overwhelm him even during Metamorphosis, and Skull Basher/Abyssal Blade paired with his attack speed deny a Sunder almost entirely -- Battle Trance also nullifies Sunder's effect if it lands.
Fervor/Battle Trance's attack speed crushes Tombstone fast, and his frontline, no-disable playstyle makes him easy prey.

96.note: Battery Assault easily interrupts his poor cast animation, and Power Cogs negates Stampede.
Kinetic Field and Glimpse both completely negate Stampede.
X Marks the Spot negates Stampede.
Feast punishes his high health and low armor and offsets Retaliate's return damage, and an active Rage protects against Hoof Stomp, Double Edge, and Stampede.

Moon Glaives rarely trigger Retaliate directly, her common lifesteal items offset it further, Eclipse punishes a Blink Dagger-Hoof Stomp initiation, and her natural Black King Bar blocks his whole kit except Retaliate -- though Hood/Pipe or Blade Mail give him real answers back.
His high health and rare Linken's or Black King Bar make him a great Reaper's Scythe target, and Heartstopper Aura punishes high-health heroes hard -- though Hood/Pipe blunt it.
He has no way to punish Refraction, which negates his whole burst, and Psionic Traps give vision that makes initiating on her hard.

Neither his kit nor his nukes threaten Centaur much, Hoof Stomp's AoE stun and damage hits both him and Tempest Double at once, and Stampede easily catches his no-escape kit -- though a common Gleipnir gives Arc Warden a real answer.
Stampede lets a Doomed ally simply run away, wasting the ultimate.

His low intelligence blunts Mind Flare, a well-timed Hoof Stomp usually outlasts Spiked Carapace's stun, and Blink Dagger plus detection lets him devastate a burrowed Nyx -- though Nyx can flip the fight by pre-casting Spiked Carapace and initiating with Vendetta himself, reflecting Retaliate for a stun before an Impale finish.
Swashbuckle on him procs Retaliate repeatedly, Stampede lets his team dodge Rolling Thunder easily, and his tankiness resists a late-game burst attempt.

Hoof Stomp-Double Edge bursts her down early-mid, Retaliate makes the lane nearly unwinnable for her, Stifling Dagger even triggers it and Blur can't dodge it, and his usual armor items make her attacks tickle -- though Aghanim's Fan of Knives can disable Retaliate through spell immunity.

His illusions kill themselves fast to Retaliate, Hoof Stomp/Double Edge clear a big chunk of them, his small mana pool blunts Diffusal Blade's drain once it's empty though Double Edge is free, and Hoof Stomp's slow cast time is easy to dodge with Doppelganger.

His mobility items and Stampede-hasted speed plus high health make him very hard to kill from range, punishing Sniper with Retaliate and a common Blade Mail, while Sniper's own low health and no escape make him easy prey for Hoof Stomp-Double Edge.
Focus Fire's attack-speed boost against his high health and low damage output makes Retaliate deal massive damage back, and Windrun's evasion doesn't stop his mostly-magic kit from demolishing her.

97.note: Chemical Rage lets him survive Reverse Polarity's stun with regen to spare, blunting Magnus's damage.

Counterspell's magic resistance helps him survive Reverse Polarity, and if Skewer/RP whiff or get shrugged off, Magnus is left with nothing to answer a Blink counter-initiate or escape -- Mana Break drains his much-needed mana on top of it.
Rupture deals extra damage during a Skewer or Force Staff, denying the escape or counter-initiate and forcing an early Linken's.
Thunder Strike disables his Blink Dagger for a long window, Glimpse pulls him back after a Skewer or Force Staff escape, and Static Storm denies Reverse Polarity right after he jumps in.

Empower doesn't let him win a manfight against Berserker's Blood's attack speed and regen and his big health, and from range Huskar can punish an initiation attempt with Life Break/Burning Spear denying Blink Dagger.
His damage-over-time keeps Blink Dagger on cooldown, and Macropyre both denies the initiation and destroys trees to reveal him hiding.
Reduced vision at night makes initiating hard, and Aghanim's Void plus a Gem often finds him first for a Crippling Fear silence.

Illusory Orb scouts him out hiding in trees, Phase Shift dodges a well-timed Shockwave, Waning Rift/Dream Coil counter-initiate after a Reverse Polarity-Skewer combo, Dream Coil denies casting Skewer entirely, and her own Blink Dagger makes her hard to lock down unless targeted directly.
He usually plays from range ready to Sun Ray, and can counter-initiate with his full kit even after eating Reverse Polarity-Skewer.

Plasma Field-plus-Eye of the Storm slows can lock down Blink Dagger before he initiates, Static Link drains Empower's bonus damage though Skewer/Force Staff break the link, and Storm Surge lets his team dodge Shockwave/Reverse Polarity.
His whole kit is easy Spell Steal fodder, especially Reverse Polarity for a counter-initiate, and Telekinesis is one of the best instant disables to ruin his engage.
Shrapnel can scout him out and put Blink Dagger on cooldown, though his backline positioning makes him hard to reach with Reverse Polarity without prior vision.
Haunt disables his Blink Dagger, and she can usually outlive Reverse Polarity's duration late-game.
Eyes in the Forest scouts him hiding in trees to disrupt an initiation, and Overgrowth directly counters his engage.

March of the Machines/Heat-Seeking Missile put Blink Dagger on cooldown, forcing a Skewer/Force Staff engage instead, Defense Matrix, spreadable via Rearm, shortens Reverse Polarity's duration, and his own Blink Dagger makes him hard to lock down unless targeted directly.
Plague Ward scouts him hiding in trees and denies Blink Dagger at the same time.
Even if he dies to a Magnus combo, Reincarnation means his whole team stays slowed and vulnerable to a counter-initiate.
Thundergod's Wrath/Lightning Bolt find him hiding in trees, letting allies react before the initiation lands.
His whole kit is excellent against the Phantasm illusion army.
His and Empower's AoE damage and disables punish a clumped clone swarm hard.
Reverse Polarity pierces Rage, wasting part of its duration, and his tankiness and mobility make him hard for Lifestealer to pin down and kill at any stage.

98.note: Brain Sap's pure damage ignores Reactive Armor stacks, Nightmare denies a Timber Chain escape for a chain-stun setup, Enfeeble cuts his regen from the armor hard, and Fiend's Grip pierces Black King Bar to drain his low mana and immobilize him.
Doom shuts off his mobility and damage entirely, breaking Reactive Armor's Aghanim's bonuses too, and Infernal Blade's repeated stuns can interrupt Timber Chain while scaling with his high HP.
Searing Chains denies Timber Chain, and Fire Remnant/Flame Guard's magic burst punishes him hard since his own pure-damage kit can't remove Flame Guard.

Time Dilation acts like a long silence that makes him useless or forces an item-build pivot, Time Walk negates his burst, Time Lock's magic damage and lockdown beats both Reactive Armor and Timber Chain, and Chronosphere plus Time Lock can kill him before he reacts while also blocking Timber Chain's escape route.
He's completely helpless against Phantom's Embrace once Chakram is on cooldown.
Cold Snap's repeated stuns interrupt Timber Chain/Chakram's long casts and can stop him mid-chain, and his late-game magic and pure damage bypasses Timbersaw's armor easily.
Hex cripples his mobility, an Earth Spike-Mana Drain follow-up denies a Timber Chain escape, and Finger of Death finishes him at low HP.
Heartstopper Aura negates his big HP pool and regen, Death Pulse plus creep-kill sustain helps allies survive his burst, and standing in the thick of fights makes him easy Reaper's Scythe bait.
Arcane Orb's pure damage bypasses Reactive Armor, and Sanity's Eclipse still hits him inside an Astral Imprisonment, finishing him before Timber Chain saves him while draining his escape mana.
Rolling Thunder's stuns make escaping via Timber Chain much harder.
Nether Ward punishes his low-cooldown spell spam hard, and his lack of any stun or silence leaves him with no answer to Life Drain, worse combined with Decrepify.
Hex cripples his mobility, and Shackles' stun-plus-damage-over-time undercuts his Reactive Armor regen.
His long-range, low-cooldown nukes harass Timbersaw out of lane easily.

Arcane Curse stacks damage every cast since he relies on constant ability use, Glaives of Wisdom's pure damage plus intelligence steal punishes his mana-hungry playstyle, and Last Word/Global Silence both interrupt his combo or shut him down entirely.
Ball Lightning makes him hard to chase even for a mobile Timbersaw, and Static Remnant/Overload let Storm burst him down even mid-escape.
Meld breaks his armor to expose him to Reactive Armor bypass, and Refraction resists Whirling Death's damage -- though Chakram burns through Refraction fast.
Viper Strike denies Reactive Armor stacking entirely.
His huge magic burst is among the best early answers to Timbersaw, and Lightning Bolt's ministun interrupts a Timber Chain escape.
Reactive Armor resists Tidebringer's physical damage almost entirely, and Whirling Death's strength reduction forces him off the lane or into buying Tangoes.

Spiderlings barely dent Reactive Armor and die fast to his AoE, her only mobility is Spin Web's speed buff which Timber Chain easily escapes, and his tree-cutting denies her hiding spots near the map's edges.

Whirling Death's stacking strength reduction cuts his durability hard, Blade Mail can't touch an attribute change and Timber Chain just waits it out, Reactive Armor blunts Culling Blade's threshold, and Chakram's disarm shuts off Counter Helix while his pure damage ignores all of Axe's armor sources.
Reactive Armor tanks a Chaos Bolt-Reality Rift combo, and his pure-damage AoE clears the Phantasm army fast.
Clumped clones are easy prey for his area abilities, though Earthbind denies a Timber Chain escape.
He can cut down the tree Monkey King's standing in for a long stun, and Timber Chain escapes Wukong's Command/Primal Spring's slow -- though Jingu Mastery can still harass him out of a mid lane.
He easily cuts down Sprout's trees to deny a Teleportation escape or trap, clears treants fast, and Reactive Armor lets him tank their damage while healing off it.
Reactive Armor sustains through Stifling Dagger harass and ganks, her all-physical Blur does nothing against his spells, and Timber Chain lets him disengage easily.

His constant low-burst attacks max Reactive Armor almost instantly, Timber Chain then makes him nearly unkillable, and Whirling Death/Chakram instantly clear illusion groups -- though a late-game Diffusal Blade is a real problem.
His mostly-physical late-game damage struggles against a mobile Timbersaw, and he rarely right-clicks so Static Link steals little.

Chakram scouts him out if he Pounces into trees, none of Timbersaw's abilities need a target so they still hit him in Shadow Dance, Reactive Armor's regen can't be stolen by Essence Shift, and Timber Chain lets him actually give chase.
His area burst clears illusions fast, and Reactive Armor plus another armor item cuts a big chunk of Terrorblade's damage.
His tree-cutting kit levels whole sections of forest, denying Treant's hiding spots, and he can cut down an Eyes in the Forest tree even without meaning to.

99.note: Mana Break starves the mana his abilities need in lane, and Blink dodges him entirely or lets Anti-Mage get in front of him for a fight.
Infernal Blade punishes his high health, and Doom locks out his low-cooldown spells, denying Warpath, with the Break talent stripping his damage reduction passive too.
Time Dilation stops him from spamming his low-cooldown kit, Chronosphere lets allies reposition to hit him from the front, bypassing his rear damage reduction, and he has no way to stop a Time Walk.
Phantom's Embrace silences Viscous Nasal Goo/Quill Spray, and Ink Swell's stun plus speed boost lets allies get in front of him to bypass his passive.
Sharpshooter deals massive damage and long disables his passive, and Bushwhack/Scurry both kite him easily.
Duel forces him to face her head-on, denying his rear damage reduction entirely, and Press the Attack dispels stacked Viscous Nasal Goo slows.
Reaper's Scythe and Heartstopper Aura both deal percent-health damage that ignores his high health, and Heartstopper's drain doesn't even trigger his passive.
His burst ignores the damage-reduction passive entirely even from the front, and Astral Imprisonment cuts his mana while letting OD reposition in front of him for a full-damage Sanity's Eclipse.

Eye of the Storm melts his armor, Static Link fully drains his Warpath bonus damage, and Storm Surge lets Razor outrun even a stacked Viscous Nasal Goo slow -- a Shard Eye of the Storm even deals full damage every time he faces Razor to cast his own slow.

Arcane Curse stacks every cast, forcing him to either stop spamming or take heavy degeneration, Glaives of Wisdom's intelligence steal causes real mana problems, and Last Word/Global Silence shut his kit off entirely.
Guardian Sprint outruns him even under a stacked slow, and Corrosive Haze's armor reduction cuts his tankiness hard.

Essence Shift lets him hit Bristleback freely from any angle while stripping his stats, Pounce disengages to heal off Essence Shift's passive before returning already-weakened, Dark Pact nearly always clears the Viscous Nasal Goo stack though not Quill Spray's damage, and he commonly buys the Silver Edge that directly counters him.
Whirling Death both damages him and cuts his strength for less tankiness, Reactive Armor sustains through his stacks, and Timber Chain outruns even a slowed chase.
Nethertoxin disables his passive outright, and Viper Strike/Poison Attack's slows keep him from escaping the Nethertoxin zone.
Shukuchi repositions in front of him to deny the rear-damage passive, and a Mana Break talent drains the mana his spam kit needs.
Quill Spray destroys her spiderlings and still hits her even while she regens in Spin Web, making him one of her hardest lane counters.
Quill Spray quickly destroys his Phantasm illusions.
Turning away from him cuts Burning Spear's damage, and baiting a Life Break jump then turning around punishes him hard.
Macropyre's frequent ticks trigger his passive repeatedly for free damage as long as he keeps his back turned.
His wolves deal little damage and die fast to Quill Spray even invisible, and his lack of burst makes killing Bristleback from behind very hard.
Quill Spray usually hits several clones at once, though he can't turn his back while rooted by Earthbind.

His tankiness and rear-damage reduction make him very hard for Phantom Lancer's low-burst kit to finish, Quill Spray shreds the illusion army fast, and his passive costs no mana so a Diffusal Blade mana drain doesn't stop it.
He's one of the hardest heroes to gank with Meat Hook-Dismember, and the attempt sometimes backfires on Pudge.

Quill Spray hits him even while invisible, Cloak and Dagger's backstab bonus is irrelevant against him, Smoke Screen doesn't stop his passive from triggering, and his natural tankiness makes him an ideal Gem carrier to directly counter Riki's invisibility.
His kit is nearly worthless to steal since Rubick gains no Warpath value from casting instead of attacking.
Quill Spray hits him inside his own Sand Storm and puts Blink Dagger on cooldown to deny an escape, and Epicenter's many ticks repeatedly trigger his passive during fights.
Quill Spray combined with a Blade Mail easily triggers off Focus Fire's damage.
